News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta virtually confirms new contract extension with Arsenal manager set for huge pay rise
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA told Arsenal fans not to worry after virtually confirming he will extend his Emirates contract.

The Gunners boss is into the final 12 months of his deal but will land a pay rise on his £10million-a-year salary.



Arsenal, who want to tie Arteta down after he led them to Prem glory last season, face Manchester City in the Community Shield in Cardiff tomorrow.

Arteta said: “The fans don’t have to worry about any of that, because I want to be here. I am extremely happy.



“I feel very grateful to work with the people that I work with and when we have the possibility, we will resolve that. And that’s it.

“There is always another priority!



“That’s the way we have been treating it because everybody feels comfortable that the time on the contract is not going to be an issue.

“My will, certainly, is to be here and I am very happy here. My feeling from the club’s the same. That’s why everyone is doing things in a really organic way.”

The Gunners are keen to add an attacker but Arteta has been shocked by the big transfer fees this summer, with target Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea for £117million.

Asked if he was surprised by the big fees in the window, Arteta said: “Yes. I wouldn’t have bet.

“That’s the market. That means there are clubs happy to invest or they believe that the valuations of those players are that, and that’s fair.”

Arteta refused to discuss Arsenal’s interest in Konsa and Quansah, but gave a positive fitness update ahead of Sunday.

Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi all missed Wednesday’s friendly with Como, however they are set to be in the squad to face City.

Arteta said: “They will be available. They will train, and if they are in the condition that we expect them to be, they will be involved.”

Jurrien Timber will miss the game, however, due to a groin issue that has plagued him since March.



The Arsenal boss added: “He is progressing really well, he is on the pitch.

“We are ramping up now with certain actions and especially the volume and the load.

“He is on a good trajectory, but there are still a few weeks to go. William [Saliba], as we all know, it’s more a long-term injury.”

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star Francis Coquelin, 35, rushed to hospital after sickening head clash as ‘Red Cross intervene’
Sports.content:
Add us as a preferred source

OUCH! Former Arsenal star Francis Coquelin, 35, rushed to hospital after sickening head clash as ‘Red Cross intervene’

FORMER Arsenal star Francis Coquelin has been rushed to hospital after a horrific head clash while playing for French Ligue 2 side, Laval.

The brutal scene even saw the French Red Cross get involved, according to reports.



Laval midfielder Coquelin and Nantes man Wilitty Younoussa violently collided heads early on in the second game of the league campaign.

It was a heartbreaking moment for the ex-Arsenal man, as his first start since rejoining his boyhood club was cut very short.



Volunteer medics from the French Red Cross were called onto the field of play before the Frenchman was rushed off to hospital.

Following the incident, French reporter Cyprien Legeay wrote: “Major concern in Laval after Francis Coquelin and Wilitty Younoussa violently collided with their heads.



“The players quickly made big gestures to get the Red Cross to intervene quickly.”

Later reports suggest he’s getting a scan, with bleeding and a fracture suspected.

The 35-year-old’s Laval career has been brought to a gutting halt if reports turn out to be true.

He played for the Northern French team between 2005-2008 as a youngster before earning a move to Premier League giants Arsenal.



While he never made a senior appearance for the club, they played a huge part in his development.

And today’s injury won’t have done him any favours in attempting to repay them.

The clash with Nantes ended in a 2-1 win for Laval after a 95th minute winner.

However, according to reports coming out of France, a storm knocked out the broadcast towards the end of the clash.

This reportedly forced broadcasters to film with phones at the end of a dramatic night in the North West.



The victory takes them up to tenth in Ligue 2 after losing their season opener to Rodez.

Sports.title: Arsenal lead £51m transfer race for England U21 star Jack Hinshelwood but could face Man Utd competition
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are leading the race to sign Jack Hinshelwood from Brighton.

The 21-year-old has become a top priority for the Gunners ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.



Arsenal officials have already made direct contact with Hinshelwood‘s representatives over a potential move and are preparing an official bid.

Mikel Arteta believes the midfielder could be the perfect addition to his squad.



Hinshelwood can play in the centre of midfield, holding midfield and in both full-back positions.

His versatility has made him a major target for Arteta, who has previously favoured stars who can play in more than one position.



However, the Gunners face competition from two key rivals in the race for the Brighton ace.

Manchester United have held a longstanding interest in Hinshelwood and have made official inquiries to check his availability.

The Red Devils are planning their own move in the coming days to challenge Arsenal.

Manchester City are also understood to be considering a swoop for the England U21 star.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

A glowing review on Hinshelwood from the club’s scouting department is expected to prompt informal preliminary inquiries with Brighton to assess terms.

While the Seagulls would prefer to keep their academy graduate, it’s believed that a bid within the range of £43million to £51m could lead to an agreement.

Hinshelwood – the son of ex-Brighton star Adam Hinshelwood – still has three years left on his contract, putting Brighton in a strong negotiating position.

The midfielder has made 79 senior appearances since breaking into the first team in 2023.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star Lucas Torreira, 30, ‘asks to leave Galatasaray after second incident with stalker who assaulted him’
Sports.content:
FORMER Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira has reportedly asked to leave Galatasaray following a second incident with a stalker in Turkey.

The 30-year-old was assaulted at an Istanbul shopping centre in May.



A man allegedly punched him outside a cafe and was caught by police after attempting to flee in a taxi.

Local reports claimed that Torreira had a pre-existing restraining order against the individual, who had already made threats towards him.



The perpetrator was eventually jailed, but new reports claim that he was released this week and began threatening the midfielder again.

Journalist Sebastian Giovanelli claims that Torreira has now asked his agent to get him out of Turkey.



The latest threat allegedly saw the perpetrator approach Torreira’s driver and say: “I’m here to finish what I started.”

Turkish police are now looking for him once again.

Torreira joined Galatasaray from Arsenal in 2022 and has since made 175 appearances.

The midfielder has also managed 11 goals and 16 assists during his time in Turkey and won six trophies.



Prior to that, he spent four years with Arsenal, where he played 89 times.

Torreira was also loaned out twice to Atletico Madrid and Fiorentina by the north London side.

Sports.title: England star, 32, was offered a place at Harvard University before taking up footie career
Sports.content:
PATRICK BAMFORD would choose a freezing, rain-lashed night at Burnley or Stoke over the ivory towers of Harvard every single day of the week.

The Sheffield United striker has zero regrets about snubbing America’s most famous university to take up a career in football.



For him the brutal, bruising war of the Championship beats a fancy economics degree.

And Bamford, 32, has a clear promotion message for Blades fans ahead of the gruelling new campaign.



He said: “We’re going to try everything we can to go up.

“And the fans should just know that’s what all the players are aiming for and what we’re hopefully heading towards.”



Forget the high-society lecture halls and quiet libraries. The forward has famous brains as well as footballing brawn.

He famously turned down the chance to study at Ivy League giants Harvard back in the day.

But when the winter grind kicks in, he never wishes he was sitting in a warm Massachusetts classroom instead.

Asked if studying in America ever sounds more appealing during three-game weeks, Bamford was brutally honest.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He said: “No, I think that as bad as it sounds, that was always my back-up plan.

“It might sound silly not to want to go to one of the world’s top universities — but I always wanted to be a footballer from as young as I can remember.”

It takes a serious work ethic to make it to the very top. And Bamford had to strike a strict deal with his parents to chase his sporting dream.

He revealed: “I always had a promise with my mum and dad that they’d support me in football as long as I always got my A-levels. And I got good results.



“And yes, that was the deal. And it was something I had to stick to until I was 18. But football was really always the dream.”

And now, that dream is all about getting back to the promised land of the Premier League.

The gruelling 46-game slog of the Championship is notoriously one of the hardest in world football.

It takes much more than just silky skills and expensive squads to get over the line.

Bamford, who joined the Blades in November, knows exactly what it takes to escape the second-tier rat race.



He explained: “Normally it’s the teams that have the mentality to turn a loss into a draw or draw into a win.

“And even when it’s not pretty, achieve a good result.”

That grit is forged deep inside the dressing-room walls. Tactics are great, but team spirit and raw passion are what truly win titles.

Bamford said: “You need a few vocal leaders in the dressing room to keep everyone on song.

“And you must keep everyone pushing in the same direction.”



On the pitch, the mission for any frontman is simple: score goals.

And the star has a very straightforward philosophy when it comes to hitting the back of the net.

It is not about over complicating things or waiting for the perfect tactical blueprint.

Bamford said: “I think that you need to find yourself in between the posts — goal side of the penalty spot.



“Try and finish the attack in the middle of the goal.

“Because you’d be amazed just by being in there, you seem to be in the right place all the time.”

It is a clever knack that separates the good strikers from the great ones.

He added: “Sometimes it gets there and sometimes it doesn’t. But you’d be amazed how many easy goals you get from just being in the right place.

“I think that’s something you kind of learn as you gain experience.”



Modern football relies heavily on technology and complex data.

Managers and analysts spend hours breaking down every single movement on the pitch.

But the savvy forward likes to keep things sharp and focused.

Former Middlesbrough and Leeds star Bamford explained: “I’d look at the other team before and see where the chances are coming from. I’m going to look for isolation during the game.

“I’m analysing chances — just seeing what I could do better. What I think I did wrong or what decision I made that was wrong.”



Yet the one-cap England man, who played against Andorra in 2021, knows you cannot ever let the bad days linger in your mind.

He added: “There are also some games where I just seem to forget about it all. It’s not always going to go your way.”

Away from the pitch, finding a proper balance is completely vital.

The mental pressure of the game can easily weigh players down.

Bamford admits it is almost impossible to fully switch off from the sport.



He said: “I think it’s important to have other aspects to your life.

“Other things that take your mind off football. But it is very hard to not have your mind on football all the time.”

The summer break offers only a tiny window of peace.

He added: “You only really truly have a little bit of time away from thinking football for the first two weeks or so of the off season.

“And then after that you’re thinking about starting to do stuff to get yourself ready for pre-season. You don’t have that much time.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

To cope, the former Nottingham Forest academy kid looks for distractions.

He said: “I think having hobbies and other things that maybe direct your attention sometimes will help.”

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso was right to pick Chelsea over Liverpool – it’s an easier job for him, says Glen Johnson
Sports.content:
EX-LIVERPOOL and Chelsea ace Glen Johnson claims Xabi Alonso was right to take over at Stamford Bridge rather than Anfield.

Johnson, 41, spent four years with the Blues as former owner Roman Abramovich’s first ever signing in 2003 before his move to the Reds where he underwent a six-year stint until 2015.



The former England international signed with the Merseysiders in 2009, which was the same year Alonso, 44, left the Kop for Real Madrid after a glittering five-year spell.

Many expected the Spanish tactician to return to Liverpool as manager this summer when former boss Arne Slot looked set to exit.



That was after the former midfielder turned down the chance to replace Jurgen Klopp in 2024 as he opted to stay at Bayer Leverkusen after leading them to an undefeated maiden Bundesliga title and domestic Double.

But Alonso ended up going to Chelsea before Slot’s departure from Liverpool, despite a chaotic 2025/26 campaign that included three managerial changes and a tenth-placed finish in the Premier League.

And the ex-Real manager wasn’t daunted about becoming the club’s fifth permanent hire since BlueCo took over in 2022 from Abramovich.

Chelsea, however, appointed him as manager, which means the ex-Leverkusen boss gets a huge say in the team’s direction, structure and transfers.

Liverpool, on the other hand, were looking for a head coach to replace Slot before Andoni Iraola’s arrival, which means Alonso would have had far less influence at Anfield.

And Johnson is adamant the Spain legend made the right call as there will be far less pressure to deal with at Chelsea.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The former full-back believes he would be facing significantly higher demands to deliver at Liverpool due to his legendary status, just like he did at Real which led to a sorry eight-month stint.

Johnson told SunSport on behalf of SeatPin: “I’m not surprised so many people think he should have been Liverpool manager.

“He’s a Liverpool legend and one of the best midfielders to ever wear a Liverpool shirt, but that doesn’t mean he should manage them.

“The extra pressure of being a club legend from your playing days when you manage there adds extra pressure.

“I think it’s easier for him to be Chelsea manager rather than Liverpool manager. Alonso won’t want to tarnish his reputation with Liverpool fans if it doesn’t work out for him managing there, as he did at Real Madrid.



“He’s still a young manager, so I think avoiding Liverpool for now is sensible for him.

“Chelsea is a fantastic football club that has already backed him in the transfer market, and as long as the team performs, his job will be safe.”

Johnson was also “perplexed” by another Chelsea addition as he found it “strange” that Morgan Rogers snubbed Premier League champions Arsenal for a British record £117million move to Stamford Bridge.



The ex-West Ham ace insists this was a very successful signing for the Blues but admitted his former club may have “overpaid”.

Johnson added: “I think it was a strange decision by Morgan Rogers to sign for Chelsea over Arsenal.

“I’m not sure why Rogers chose Chelsea over the reigning champions who are likely to compete for the title next season. Arsenal’s loss is Chelsea’s gain, though.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The fee was a lot of money, and I’m not sure his talent has yet justified that type of money. He’s obviously a great player, and he is still young with plenty of time to develop into a player worth that much money.

“I hope he proves me wrong, but I think Chelsea overpaid for Rogers and I’m perplexed as to why he chose Chelsea over Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Jimenez salvages dramatic point for Wolves on Molineux return
Sports.content:
Raul Jimenez scored a stoppage-time equaliser from the penalty spot on his return to Molineux to salvage a 2-2 draw for Wolves against Blackburn.

Wolves took the lead through Marshall Munetsi when Fer Lopez threaded the ball through for him to finish neatly beyond Balazs Hoth. But Blackburn scored a deserved equaliser when Sean McLoughlin nodded in from Ryoya Morishita's right-wing cross.

And Rovers stunned most of the 30,984 inside Molineux when Andri Gudjohnsen converted from close range early in the second half. Wolves turned to returning hero Jimenez off the bench but there was very little sign of them finding an equaliser.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Curtis Davies and Jobi McAnuff debate whether Wolves' late penalty was correctly awarded

That changed when Jackson Tchatchoua's left-wing cross struck the hand of the otherwise excellent Ryan Alebiosu just inside the box and the referee awarded a penalty. Jimenez held his nerve to snatch a point for Cesar Peixoto's Wolves side.

It was barely deserved. Tony Mowbray's Blackburn, unfancied going into the campaign before a ball was kicked, could not hold on for the victory but did exceed expectations. Wolves will need to improve significantly if they are to come close to satisfying theirs.

Jimenez: We need to learn from this

Image: Jimenez scores Wolves' late equaliser from the penalty spot

Wolves hero Raul Jimenez speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's amazing to be back, scoring in the first game of the season. It's not the result we were looking for in our first home game of the new season, so we need to learn from this. All the games are going to be difficult here, no matter who we play against.

"We need to keep going, it's just the start. I'm going to keep working and going forward to keep improving with the team, to hopefully earn many points and score a lot of goals."

On giving out free 'Si Senor' scarves to the Wolves supporters in the Sir Jack Hayward Stand:

"It's nice to give them back some love that they were showing me for the past eight years, even when I wasn't here at the club. I felt the big love they had for me, so it's the least I could do."

Peixoto: We played with heart not head

Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's not the result we wanted, we wanted to win. We were better in the first half, we created a lot of situations but didn't score. In the second half we suffered a bit more, we conceded the goal.

"But the effort of the players was good. We showed big heart to fight until the end. We want to be a team who never gives up, but we have to improve and stay organised."

Sports.title: Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as Werro wins 800m gold
Sports.content:
Britain's Keely Hodgkinson was denied a hat-trick of European 800m golds

Keely Hodgkinson came up just short of a coveted European 800m title hat-trick after Swiss favourite Audrey Werro won their hotly-anticipated showdown in Birmingham as the British Olympic champion settled for silver.

Hodgkinson started quicker but was overtaken by Werro on the back straight and the latter was never overtaken after the first 200m.

Double-defending champion Hodgkinson was just behind as they rounded the final bend, but Werro would not be caught and crossed the finish in a championship record 1:54.81.

Werro, Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol finished first, second and third in the highly-anticipated 800m final

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Hodgkinson claimed silver in 1:55.01 and the Netherlands' Femke-Broeders Bol took bronze in a national record 1:55.54.

After losing her title, Hodgkinson said: "Mixed emotions. With that level of competition, any medal is an achievement.

"I thought I was going to win. I didn't do anything wrong, just one of those things.

"I've had a pretty good day today, just didn't go the way that I wanted.

"There were so many different ways that could have played out and we'd figure it out after the first 100m. Audrey wanted to take it on and with that wind I was happy to let her. We're all really great athletes so I knew it was going to be close. I'm looking forward to the next match-up.

"I've said all year it's really motivating to be in such a competitive event. I love it, it brings out the best in me. Championship racing, that's what it's all about, you don't know how it's going to go and some people can have a good day or a bad day. I had a pretty good day today but it just didn't go how I wanted it to."

The world record remains the longest-standing record in athletics set in 1983 by Jarmila Kratochvilova's with a time of 1:53.28 seconds.

While the world record wasn't troubled, Werro's time of 1:54.81 did break the championship record set by Olga Mineyeva in 1982.

Hodgkinson's silver medal is Britain's 10th medal in five days on home soil. Earlier on Friday, Zharnel Hughes claimed silver in the men's 200m.

Sports.title: Arteta says he will sign new Arsenal contract in 'organic way'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed he will sign a new Arsenal contract and there is no need for fans to be worried about his future.

Arteta has entered the final year of his contract with the Premier League champions - despite co-chairman Josh Kroenke saying in May that a new deal was an "upmost priority" of the club.

But Arteta says he and the club will come together to "resolve" a contract extension in "an organic way" - because he is happy at the club, and his bosses appear happy with him.

"They [the fans] don't have to worry about any of that because I want to be here, I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with," said Arteta about his contract talks.

"When we have the possibility, we will resolve that. That's it.

"Everybody feels comfortable that the timing of the contract is not going to be an issue because my will certainly is to be here and I'm very happy here. My feeling from the club is the same one. That's why everyone is doing things in a very organic way."

Does Arteta have enough attacking firepower this season?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arteta says the transfer window still offers an opportunity to evolve and does not rule out players joining or leaving the club

Arteta also addressed questions about whether his team have enough firepower this season to reclaim the Premier League title - and win the other competitions as well.

Despite winning the Premier League and reaching the Champions League final, Arteta's Arsenal were accused of not being too attacking last term - although there was praise for their defensive solidity.

Arsenal have added Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis to their midfield and attack this season - having sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas.

Apart from that, the Gunners have mostly the same midfielders and forwards that ended last season - despite showing an interest in Vinicius Junior, Julian Alvarez and Bradley Barcola in the attacking areas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Savundra takes a closer look at the numbers of Arsenal target Victor Osimhen

Asked if he has enough attacking quality up front at the moment, Arteta replied: "If they are fit, yes.

"But when you look last year at the amount of days, games, months that we missed a lot of our important players and players with a lot of goal threat, the manner that we sustained to have the season that we had, I think is remarkable.

"It talks about the team playing and conducting, and I think it's something that the team deserves credit for.

"We're going to prefer to elevate our level, for sure, expecting that the rest will do the same, because that's traditionally what happened in the league in the last few years. And that's what we have planned this season, and we want to evolve it.

"I have to prepare a team that is capable of winning in whatever the context is: because we're not good enough on the day, because the opponent is so good, because the differences in games. That's my job, that's how I will prepare the team."

Sports.title: Super Giants storm into Hundred men's final by beating SunRisers
Sports.content:
The Manchester Super Giants set up a meeting with Trent Rockets in The Hundred final after beating SunRisers Leeds by 20 runs in the men's eliminator at The Kia Oval.

The Super Giants were given a brilliant platform after a swashbuckling 114-run partnership - including 13 sixes - between opener Paul Walter (80 off 46) and Heinrich Klaasen (63 off 26) propelled their side to an imposing total of 186-4 from their 100 balls.

The work of Harry Brook (49 off 31) and Ryan Rickelton (54no off 34) gave SunRisers hope, but the excellent bowling of Josh Tongue (4-26) against a fearsome top order brought Leeds' 2026 Hundred campaign to a close and secured his side's place in Sunday's final at Lord's, starting at 6pm live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook was harshly given out lbw after scoring 49

Tongue dismantles SunRisers' top order to seal Super Giants' win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England seamer Brydon Carse strikes second ball for Sunrisers Leeds, claiming the big wicket of New Zealand star Tim Seifert

SunRisers got off to a flying start when Brydon Carse took the wicket of dangerman Tim Seifert - who smashed 80 off 40 balls against the same opposition three days ago - with the second ball of the contest.

Jos Buttler (33 off 20) steadied the ship, though, putting on a fifty stand with Walter in a useful cameo that got his side back on track, before the swashbuckling Klaasen and Walter combined for their incredible partnership to set their opponents 187 to win.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler was dismissed by Matt Potts after smashing a six off the previous ball

SunRisers opener Mitch Marsh (10 off 6) made a quick start, smashing boundaries in successive balls off Gus Atkinson's first five, but the explosive Tongue tempted him into an ill-advised top edge, and the dismissal of skipper Zak Crawley (6 off 3) followed when Tongue trapped him in front just four balls later.

The batting side regained momentum as Brook and Rickelton combined well in an 81-run stand, but Brook's hopes of a quick fifty were dashed by a contentious Sonny Baker (2-39) lbw - replays showed the delivery was outside the line, but the SunRisers were out of reviews, leaving Brook helpless.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue took two wickets in four balls for the Super Giants to check the SunRisers' progress

Leeds were reeling after Dan Lawrence (2) and Matt Revis (4) were dismissed by brilliant catches by Leus du Plooy and Seifert respectively, and more outstanding bowling from Tongue and spinner Liam Dawson sealed what turned into a comfortable 20-run win to take the Super Giants one step closer to The Hundred title.

Buttler: Players stood up in crucial moments

Image: Paul Walter smashed 80 off 46 balls for the Super Giants

Manchester Super Giants captain Jos Buttler, speaking to Sky Sports Cricket:

"I'm really happy. So many players stood up in some crucial moments.

"Tim Seifert has been in unbelievable form, so to lose him so early was disappointing, but Paul Walter has been incredible - so for him to be the backbone of the innings and score so well, showed what he could do.

"All round with the ball we were great, finding ways to take wickets. Our Achilles heel at the start of the tournament was probably our catching, but we took some great catches.

"Trent Rockets are a top side. They've got into the final because they've been the form side throughout the tournament.

"We're in a good rhythm, but they've been able to rest up and prepare well. We'll find out [who wins] Sunday night."

Sports.title: Raúl Jiménez’s injury-time penalty salvages point for Wolves against Blackburn
Sports.content:
Raúl Jiménez marked his return to Wolves with the stoppage-time equaliser that saved them from an embarrassing start to their return to the Championship.

The Mexico striker, who scored against England during the World Cup finals, retained his composure to convert a penalty given for handball by Rayan Alebiosu that would have had VAR questioning whether the defender was in the area when Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross struck his arm. Thankfully for Wolves, the video assistant referee is no longer their problem. Jiménez, who had bought scarves for all supporters in the South Bank in gratitude for their response to welcoming him home, tucked away his first goal in this second spell for the club he graced during their recent heyday.

All that’s gold does not glisten. Wolves may have reverted to a richer sheen of their traditional colour on their return to the Championship after nine years in the Premier League, but that does not mean the gloom of relegation ends there. Cesar Peixoto’s new era in the league got off to a disappointing start as they were fortunate to gain a point off unfancied Blackburn Rovers and their former West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Mowbray.

Goals from Sean McLoughlin and Andri Gudjohnsen allowed Blackburn to provide Wolves with a reality check after Marshall Munetsi had given them an early lead. Confidence is a fragile commodity and, after their decision to replace Rob Edwards with a manager with no experience of English football, the Wolves board know that their supporters’ patience is thin. Leading Gil Vicente to sixth place in the Portuguese first division does not make Peixoto a guaranteed winner.

Molineux was awash with fading golden sunlight and rising optimism at kick-off. A summer that started with such a surprising managerial departure is promising to end with renewed faith in the team’s direction of travel, if the early noises are anything to go by.

While Wolves had organised a stash of Starbars for the head coach’s corner of the away dressing room, in honour of Tony Mowbray’s legendary love of chocolate, the returning Wolves striker Jiménez had gifted a scarf for every supporter in the South Bank. But it was the Blackburn defence who were most giving in the early stages as they split generously to allow Marshall Munetsi a clean run through onto Fer López’s sumptuous pass. The left-footed finish from the Zimbabwean, himself coming back to Molineux after a loan at Paris FC, compounded the feelgood factor buzzing around the ground.

View image in fullscreen Marshall Munetsi (right) celebrates scoring Woves’ first goal with Fer López. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Cesar Peixoto has promised to bring a front-footed high press to Wolves, since he replaced Rob Edwards as head coach, and this has been effective in pre-season and against Port Vale in the Carabao Cup. But it also leaves gaps on transition. Blackburn, who finished 20th last season and have not done so much in the transfer market to suggest they should aim higher this term, got behind Wolves on several occasions. It was no great surprise therefore when, from another superb right-wing cross from Ryoya Morishita, Sean McLoughlin, timing his run off André to perfection, headed beyond Dan Bentley to equalise.

Some of Wolves’ best business so far this summer has been bringing players back to Molineux. While Jiménez started the night on the bench, after a late start to pre-season following his impressive World Cup for Mexico, López was the classiest player on view. Back from a loan spell at Celta Vigo, he has been invited to make the No 10 position his own, and the Spaniard so nearly regained Wolves the lead only to curl his shot just wide.

Receiving Kieran Trippier’s prompt, Mateus Mané also swerved a shot just over as Wolves finished the half on the up.

View image in fullscreen Blackburn’s Andri Gudjohnsen gives his side a 2-1 lead early in the second half. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Blackburn continued to benefit from Wolves’ soft centre however. Oladapo Afolayan’s shot needed tipping over by Bentley before the right winger again got space down Wolves left – where David Møller Wolfe, the Norway left-back, was in for the injured Hugo Bueno – to cross for Andri Gudjohnsen to get in front of his man and turn in Rovers’ second goal.

By the hour mark, the South Bank were swirling their Jiménez scarves above their heads and chanting ‘Si Senor’ in honour of the veteran striker who was such an esteemed figure here at Molineux for five of the club’s best years in modern times. He was the pivotal attacking player during Nuno Espírito Santo’s reign when Wolves reached the latter stages of the FA Cup and the Europa League. The scene was set for the Mexican. Could he deliver?

Jiménez struck one free-kick into the wall, before laying an astute pass back for Tommy Doyle, though his fellow substitute could only hammer the ball over the bar after appearing to handle. It was interesting that Tripper was withdrawn, and Peixoto’s game plan was being questioned when two youngsters, in Pedro Lima and Tawanda Chirewa, were thrown on into a rejigged 4-4-2 for the final 10 minutes.

Sports.title: Europe’s top clubs threatened Club World Cup boycott before Fifa plan collapsed
Sports.content:
Europe’s leading clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless Gianni Infantino withdrew his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme, issuing their ultimatum hours before the plan was scrapped.

In a letter to the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, the influential European Football Clubs (EFC) group warned that its cooperation with future tournaments would hinge on Infantino backing down. It said the threat would hold unless a joint venture between EFC and Fifa – a framework for which has already been agreed – is completed before television rights can be sold for the 2028 Women’s Club World Cup.

The letter, dated 31 July and signed by the EFC chief executive, Charlie Marshall, said Infantino’s actions could constitute a “substantial breach” of the bodies’ existing memorandum of understanding (MoU) and suggested this could be grounds for its termination. It floated the idea that EFC and its clubs may push back against the international match calendar and its player release rules, which are crucial to ensuring national team tournaments can function. Infantino shelved the privately backed Football Forward Enterprise (FFE) in the early hours of 1 August after widespread condemnation.

Fundamental to EFC’s complaints was the impression FFE would bring all broadcasting, commercial and sponsorship rights under its own umbrella. The letter asked Fifa to confirm this and said it would take decisive action if these elements were not included in the long-proposed joint venture, whose creation is enshrined in the MoU and intended to involve managing the commercial side of global club competitions. It witheringly wrote that the tie-in had, “unlike the FFE proposal, made no meaningful progress over the past year”. EFC already has a similar joint venture with Uefa, named UC3, which was launched in 2025.

A potentially incendiary section read: “Unless a fully operational Fifa-EFC CWC joint venture, with exclusive authority over, among other things, all commercial and operational matters, is established well ahead of the women’s 2028 Fifa CWC rights cycle, EFC will not support – and its member clubs will not participate in – any future edition, including the women’s and men’s 2028 and 2029 Fifa CWC.”

In theory the threat still holds although Fifa, in a response to EFC’s letter since Infantino climbed down, is understood to have promised a swift meeting to keep the joint venture on track. EFC’s position followed concerns raised by a vast number of clubs around Europe, who were angered by the lack of consultation around the design of FFE. One major European club expressed concerns in its own letter saying it would support EFC in any “firmer collective action” if necessary and called for “more rigorous and transparent governance processes”.

Any European withdrawal from Club World Cups would in practice mean those tournaments could not run. EFC and Fifa operated last year’s Club World Cup, the first to take place with 32 teams, using a short-term prototype for any future joint venture. No hosts have yet been announced for the new-look Women’s Club World Cup or the next edition of the men’s tournament in 2029.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea won the Club World Cup in July 2025 by beating Paris Saint-Germain in the final. Photograph: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images

EFC’s letter also raised the continuing delay, first reported in February, in distributing £185m of solidarity money to clubs that did not participate in the Club World Cup. Transparency over the event’s financial performance was also requested.

“We ask that you urgently share the final surplus revenue generated by the 2025 Fifa WC, together with a full profit and loss statement, so that all revenues, expenses and costs can be properly assessed in line with our partnership in this competition,” it said. “The absence of information on this matter, as with the lack of a solution on CWC solidarity for over a year, is also of serious concern and disappointment to EFC and our member clubs.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is understood there is increasing optimism that this issue is on the verge of resolution, although a notional average £50,000 windfall for every global top-flight club, if the pot was divided equally, pales in comparison with the £84m reward long since banked by last year’s winners, Chelsea.

Referring to clubs releasing players for international duty, EFC continued: “Our memorandum of understanding, set to expire on 30 December 2030, includes EFC’s and its member clubs’ acceptance of the international match calendar and the release rules. Both are directly relevant for Fifa’s non-European member associations and to any value FFE may have.” It said Fifa’s apparent commercial vision for FFE constituted a “serious breach of trust” and warned the MoU could be jeopardised.

The letter demonstrates the extraordinary level of leverage EFC, which is chaired by the Paris Saint-Germain president, Nasser al-Khelaifi, can claim over Fifa and its increasing influence on football’s future. The organisation, set up in 2008 as a lobby group for clubs around the continent, now has well over 800 members although only a minority hold full voting rights. Some stakeholders elsewhere in football’s ecosystem have expressed fears about the level of power it has assumed. A separate representative body, the Union of European Clubs, was created in 2023 to represent smaller sides but is not recognised by Uefa.

One potential consequence of EFC’s discussions with Fifa could, in the medium term, be its expansion into a group representing clubs around the world. More immediately, last month’s letter demanded that Fifa deliver on a previous promise to fully integrate Al-Khelaifi into the Fifa council, which is purportedly its main decision-making body.

Sports.title: Liverpool owner FSG seals £1.65bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has confirmed it has agreed the sale of 30% of the club to a consortium including Amit Bhatia, the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and the Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin. The deal is understood to be worth £1.65bn, valuing Liverpool at £5.5bn, and will see Bhatia become the club’s new vice-chair on an expanded board.

Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, initiated and led talks with FSG on behalf of the 1892 Holdings consortium, a reference to Liverpool’s founding year. The former co-owner of Queens Park Rangers has received financial backing from the Mittal Family Trust, the K5 Sports fund, of which Bezos is the lead investor, and EE Capital, the family office of Elaine and Eduardo Saverin.

Elaine Saverin, wife of Eduardo, and Bryan Baum, co-founder and managing partner of K5 Global, will also join the Liverpool board. Bezos is considered a passive investor and will not have a seat on the board.

Despite the involvement of Bezos, the third richest man in the world with $272bn (£201bn), Eduardo Saverin, worth an estimated $33bn and the Mittal family, worth around $17bn, FSG will remain in operational control of Liverpool as well as majority owners. 1892 Holdings’ investment remains subject to regulatory approval, which could take up to 90 days, and will have no impact on Liverpool’s transfer budget or strategy for this summer. There is also no change to the leadership or day-to-day running of Liverpool.

FSG insist the deal is not part of an exit strategy from a club they acquired in 2010 for £300m after the near-ruinous ownership of Tom Hicks and George Gillett. The transaction does not compel FSG to sell more of the club to 1892 at a future date, or include obligations for 1892 to increase their stake, but it does give Bhatia’s consortium options to purchase more of Liverpool should the majority owners eventually decide to sell.

It is the makeup of Bhatia’s consortium, rather than any financial need, that FSG claim attracted them to the British-Indian businessman’s proposal. The FSG leadership team of principal owner John W Henry, chair Tom Werner and president Mike Gordon have spent almost a year getting to know Bhatia and believe the deal will create further opportunities for Liverpool in global business, technology and investment, including in the important markets of India and Asia.

View image in fullscreen The sale will have no impact on Liverpool’s transfer budget or strategy for this summer. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Gordon, who has resumed a more hands-on role at Liverpool following the departure of Michael Edwards as chief executive of football at FSG, said: “Liverpool has always been built by thinking beyond one season and making decisions with the club’s long-term interests in mind. That approach continues to attract interest from respected investors and business leaders around the world.

“As we considered this opportunity, it became clear that Amit and the consortium shared our long-term philosophy and appreciation for what makes Liverpool special. Their experience and perspective will complement the strong foundation already in place, and we look forward to working together.”

With Premier League and Uefa financial regulations linking a club’s spending to turnover, the new investment will not have an immediate benefit for head coach Andoni Iraola and his Liverpool team. However, the commercial opportunities presented by the involvement of Bezos, Bhatia and Saverin will enable the Anfield club to grow their annual revenue significantly. Liverpool’s annual revenue increased to a record £703m in the year ending May 2025.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Speaking on behalf of 1892 Holdings, Bhatia said: “We are incredibly proud to be investing in Liverpool Football Club and to be doing so alongside FSG. We have the utmost respect and admiration for FSG as owners and for everything they have achieved at Anfield.

“To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership, and we look forward to supporting the club’s continued success for years to come.”

Bhatia was involved in QPR for almost 19 years and took on numerous roles, from chair of the club to chair of the club’s community trust, until transferring his shareholding in July. He is likely to have a more visible presence at Anfield than fellow members of his consortium or FSG.

Sports.title: ‘Not going to be an issue’: Mikel Arteta relaxed about Arsenal contract situation
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has said he is relaxed about his Arsenal contract expiring at the end of the new season and believes his side will need to be better than last year to defend their title successfully.

The Premier League champions will face Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City in the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday and are heavy favourites to win back-to-back league titles for the first time since the 1930s. The departure of Pep Guardiola from their traditional rivals City means Arteta is now the Premier League’s longest-serving manager, with the Spaniard having joined in December 2019.

He signed a three-year contract extension in September 2024 after Arsenal finished as runners-up to City and had been expected to agree a new deal over the summer that would make him one of the highest-paid managers in the world. Arteta acknowledged on Friday that his priorities have been elsewhere this summer as he attempts to strengthen his squad before the new season but reassured supporters that he is fully committed to the club.

“They don’t have to worry about any of that, because I want to be here. I am extremely happy. I feel very grateful to work with the people that I work with and when we have the possibility, we will resolve that. And that’s it,” he said.

Asked if he expects talks over a new contract to continue after the transfer window, Arteta added: “There is always another priority, I think. And that’s the way we have been treating it, I think because everybody feels comfortable that the time on the contract is not going to be an issue. I think because my will, certainly, is to be here and I am very happy here. My feeling from the club is the same one. That is why everyone is doing things in a really organic way.”

Arsenal have opened negotiations with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they seek cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber, while they are still in the market for another attacker if they can offload Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus. After missing out on Vinícius Júnior when the Brazil forward opted to sign a new deal with Real Madrid, Arteta defended Arsenal’s strategy this summer and is hoping that they can still add to their squad.

“I am really happy with the squad, the players that I have and I am really happy with the ambition of the club. There is zero question about that. We have shown that in the manner we have tried to act,” he said.

“But I think we need to do it our own way. We have super strengths and we have other areas we need to be very conscious [of] because we don’t have the elements or the structure that other clubs have. We need to do it our way. We are always on it that way and we will do what we believe is the right thing to do. To have the best possibility to compete in every competition that’s for sure.”

Arteta added: “We’re going to prepare to elevate our level, expecting that the rest will do the same. That’s traditionally what happened in the league in the last few years, and that’s the way we have planned the season, and the way we want to evolve the team.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 10: Fulham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 15th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 11th

Prospects

Marco Silva cutting the cord after five years by the river came as little surprise. If his time at Craven Cottage was successful in re-establishing Fulham as a Premier League club, he rarely concealed his ambitions to manage in European competition. He was frequently explicit in his disappointment that the club’s ownership did not meet him halfway by funding a stronger squad. Silva’s powers of rebadging and replenishing talent will be missed now that he has decamped to Benfica. Under him, Fulham played entertaining football, a collection of ugly ducklings showing their renewed worth for a club that, despite falling short of European qualification, looked upwards rather than downwards at the relegation battle. They were often a pleasure to watch, and ornery opposition for all-comers.

Álvaro Arbeloa is a very different type of appointment, with far less experience than his predecessor in frontline coaching terms, even if he arrives with Real Madrid on his CV. His arrival, though, has opened up a working relationship with the Spanish aristos, Gonzalo García and César Palacios arriving to work with a coach who helped them through the ranks in Madrid. By little coincidence, all three share the same agency as their representatives. There have been links with Endrick and Thiago Pitarch, two further young Real jewels, leading to a sense of Fulham becoming some form of Madrileño nursery, a Santiago Bernabéu on Thames. Should that play out, it would represent another sea change.

Silva preferred to work with hard-bitten pros. A couple of his leading men, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, have departed. The latter played the best football of his career last season but, like his manager, got a better offer elsewhere, from Leeds. Fulham’s latest approach is to source young players and polish them up. Can they have the same successes as mid-tier peers such as Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth, where the approach is far more data-driven? Will supporters be looking upwards rather than downwards? A previously enigmatic club just got more enigmatic.

Off-field picture

In May, the club were runners-up at the football business awards, for stadium experience, as the Riverside Stand’s opulent hospitality completed its first full season in service. Fulham need the Riverside to deliver as a revenue stream, as financial results for the 2024-25 season showed a pre-tax loss for the year at £44.5m, and that was lowered by the sale of João Palhinha in July 2024. There has been no such windfall since. The Khan family ownership continues to back the club, its overall investment estimated at about £900m, with staff costs at 117% of turnover. Therein lies the reasoning behind Silva not receiving the backing he desired.

Owner-fan relationship

The most expensive season ticket at Craven Cottage comes in at £3,084 for access to the Riverside’s facilities, the highest in the Premier League. Shahid Khan and his son Tony, the vice-chair and director of football operations, are unpopular among committed supporters for price rises and pandering to tourism. Khan’s boat Kismet was named superyacht of the year in 2025, its main salon inspired by the Palace of Versailles, and can be chartered for more than $3m per week. Though the balance sheets confirm Khan’s outlay in funding a continued Premier League status, fans would prefer he recognised not everyone lives the high life.

The manager

Where Silva had an unremarkable playing career, Arbeloa featured among the elite, a World Cup and Champions League winner. He also had the ear of Florentino Pérez, the perennial Real Madrid president asking him to replace Xabi Alonso mid-season in the 2025-26 campaign. That did not pan out and he took his first job away from Madrid, where he was a well-regarded youth coach, in south-west London. Khan Sr’s comment that Arbeloa “believes in giving young players a chance” is pertinent for Fulham’s change in direction. Crucially, as befitting traditions at Craven Cottage, the new man from Salamanca believes in open, attacking football, offering some continuity from Silva’s reign.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García surges forward during Fulham’s Costa del Sol Trophy match against Málaga. Photograph: Joaquin Corchero/AFP7/Shutterstock

Gonzalo García’s reputation was made by his performances at last summer’s Club World Cup, where he won the tournament’s Golden Boot. Comparisons were made to Raúl, a considerable accolade at the Bernabéu. Goals followed in the Champions League against Juventus and Borussia Dortmund but García eventually lost out to the star system of Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé. His reputation in Spain is as a hard worker off the ball, necessary for a Premier League player. Last season, Rodrigo Muniz’s injuries meant the old soldier Jiménez shouldered the burden at centre-forward. García is younger and fresher but the hype surrounding his arrival gives him much to live up to.

Stat attack

Fulham had the oldest side in the Premier League last season, which may help explain why they had arguably the least intense press. Marco Silva’s side recorded the fewest high turnovers, which occur when a team recovers the ball to start a new open-play possession sequence in the final 40 metres of the pitch. Real Madrid are hardly known for being a high-pressing side but they comfortably outperformed Fulham on this metric. It will be fascinating to see how Arbeloa approaches this.

Set for a breakthrough

Jonah Kusi-Asare’s arrival last summer from Bayern Munich is further mining of a super-club’s youth department. Bayern inserted a buy-back clause for a player they picked up from AIK. The Sweden Under-21s player has been compared to Alexander Isak, and made seven substitute appearances last season – without scoring – before an initial loan became a permanent move. At 6ft 5in he offers a different profile of striker to García. Hayden Mullins, the former under-21 coach now Newport manager, saw the best of Kusi-Asare last season, the 18-year-old scoring five goals in six matches.

World Cup impact

García made his debut for Spain in a pre-World Cup friendly against Iraq but failed to make the eventual champions’ tournament squad. Antonee Robinson had a fine tournament for the USA until the co-hosts perished in the last 16 at the hands of a Belgium team featuring Timothy Castagne. Luc de Fougerolles, yet to play a Premier League game for Fulham, showed off teenage defensive talents in Canada’s run to the knockouts. To complete a successful quintet – saving the best till last? – Sander Berge had a fine tournament as Norway also reached the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: Arsenal open talks with Bayer Leverkusen over deal for Jarell Quansah
Sports.content:
Arsenal have opened talks with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they intensify efforts to bring in cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber.

The England defender, who left Liverpool last summer for an initial £30m and was part of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad, has been identified as an ideal replacement for the France and Netherlands defenders, who will miss the start of the new season due to injury. While Quansah’s preferred position is in central defence, he was also deployed at right-back by Tuchel at the World Cup and was sent off in the last-16 victory over Mexico.

It is understood that Leverkusen are reluctant to sell the Warrington-born 23-year-old, who signed a five-year deal when he left Anfield last July, and would want at least €50m (£43m). Arsenal – who saw a bid of £30m for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected earlier in the window – are not thought to want to pay that much but now could test the German club’s resolve by submitting a similar offer. Liverpool had a €70m buyback option on Quansah but that has now expired.

Arsenal are still believed to be interested in Konsa, who also filled in at right-back for England during the World Cup but is better known as a central defender. Villa value the 28-year-old at £60m.

Mikel Arteta said this week that Saliba’s back injury would take “some time to heal” and he was unsure about when he would be available again. Arsenal also have concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that forced him to miss most of the run‑in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said after Arsenal’s friendly defeat by Borussia ­Dortmund last Sunday. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.”

Arsenal would still like to sign a new attacker before the end of the window and could allow Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to depart in order to free up more funds. ­Galatasaray have offered £38m for Martinelli, although the Brazil ­forward has turned down a move to Turkey. Napoli have shown an ­interest in Jesus.

Ethan Nwaneri could also be sold, with Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund among those who have been linked with the 19-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The future of Myles Lewis-Skelly is unclear after he was offered to Chelsea and Manchester United this week. Arteta refused to address the rumours after he scored in the friendly against Como – managed by Cesc Fábregas – on Wednesday.

“I’m not going to talk about speculation,” he said. “If there is speculation about our players, it’s a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job.”

Sports.title: Chelsea expect Enzo Fernández to stay after Manchester City opt not to meet deadline
Sports.content:
Manchester City did not make a £120m bid for Enzo Fernández before Chelsea’s 5pm deadline on Friday but Enzo Maresca still expects a busy end to the transfer window, as the club seek incomings and outgoings. Chelsea, meanwhile, now expect the Argentina midfielder to stay at Stamford Bridge.

Maresca takes charge of City for the first time in a major match on Sunday against Arsenal in Cardiff in the Community Shield but is a long way from finalising the squad he will have for the season. Fernández, who played under Maresca at Chelsea, remains a target for City, who could still test the water despite missing the deadline.

“For sure there are things we need to do, how many I don’t know, can be one, can be two, depends also if players want to leave, so we can see,” Maresca said on Friday, having suggested City would not agree to Chelsea’s demands. “It’s 48 hours for the final, my first final in this club, I would like to win my first trophy, so my focus isn’t on players that can leave or players that can arrive, my focus is on the game.”

City have rejected two bids from Barcelona for Rodri but anticipate a third, and are expected to sell Tijjani Reijnders in the coming days. They are also in the market for reinforcements as they aim to challenge on four fronts. City are close to signing the 18-year-old Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille but are willing to bring in others.

Rodri, who has a year remaining on his contract, returned to the club on Friday after his holiday which followed a triumphant World Cup, but Maresca would not be drawn on the midfielder’s immediate future with a third Barcelona offer expected.

“The transfer window is open, we can buy players, we can sell players, anything can happen. I just saw Rodri now in the building, I gave him a big hug, he looks good, so we’ll see what happens.”

Reijnders is set to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Qadsiah after the two clubs agreed a £51m fee for the Dutchman, who moved to City last summer from Milan but wants more regular playing time.

“They all work every day, they all do sessions every day and at the end of the week they all want to play a game,” Maresca said. “When they don’t play they struggle to understand or they struggle to see the reason why, and I can understand that after one season some of them would like to play a little bit more. It’s a normal situation.”

James Trafford has already been sold to Leeds, while Omar Marmoush, Rico Lewis and Savinho are others who spent much of Pep Guardiola’s final season on the periphery and could be sold.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Rangers and the paradox of a painful exit that boosts their trophy chances
Sports.content:
AND NOW FOR SOME PERSPECTIVE

All new managers want to hit the ground running. But landing with a dull thud has never been a barrier to future glory, certainly not at Ibrox. Take Graeme Souness, whose start as Rangers’ player-manager put the ‘pish’ in ‘inauspicious’. On his league debut, away to Hibs, he was sent off in the first half after a revenge attack on the wrong mullet. Rangers lost 2-1 and were beaten in the third game as well. Graeme out! Rangers won the League Cup and finished the season as champions for the first time in nine years.

Dick Advocaat had a similarly awkward start in 1998. In his first game, played at Tranmere’s Prenton Park, Rangers went 3-0 down to Shelbourne in the first leg of their Big Vase tie. They went through comfortably in the end but lost the first league game a few days later. Dic- Advocaat out! Rangers had to settle for a domestic treble that season. Different times, when toys were played with for more than a few seconds before being launched from the pram with maximum force, followed a few seconds later by a handful of freshly sourced excreta. In 2026, alas, hot air and horse pucky are an acceptable substitute for reasonable discourse. And so, after failing to win any of his first four games as Rangers manager, Derek McInnes is “out of his depth” and a “dead man walking”.

Que Sera, Sera? Eff that! Turns out the future is ours to see after four games, two of them in a competition Rangers had no chance of winning anyway. Football Daily hasn’t a clue if McInnes is up to the Brobdingnagian challenge of managing Rangers, one that most tea-timely newsletters don’t really understand. But we do know that a culture of self-fulfilling poppycock, where ostentatious negativity is football’s version of the fatberg and many people would rather be right than happy, is a stain on our daily bread.

That said, what a roflcopter of a start! Given the events of last season, it was never going to be an equanimity-cultivating experience for a new Rangers manager to see Russell Martin’s start and lower it. Rangers have one point from two league games and are out of Bigger Vase after the most costly 1-1 draw against Polish opposition on British soil since Brian Clough called somebody a clown. Paradoxically, the aggregate defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok – and subsequent drop into Tin Pot – has increased Rangers’ chances of winning a trophy under McInnes. Time will tell whether those chances have increased from 0.0000001% to 0.0000002%, from 9% to 9.4% or from some other figure to some other figure. Right now, the supercomputers know, and the bairns in the prams certainly don’t.
