Sports.title: Golden girl Keely Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as British star loses her 800m European Championship crown with second-place finish - with Olympic champion jokingly removing her medal in disappointed post-race interview
Sports.content:
Audrey Werro is fast becoming an unsolvable riddle for the leading lady of British sport. For the second time in 10 weeks, this Swiss phenomenon left Keely Hodgkinson staring at her heels in a race that lived up to its billing as the best of the European Championships.

To the most talented Audrey since Hepburn went the 800m gold medal. To Hodgkinson, there was presumably no silver lining to be found in finishing a close second on home soil.

If there is to be any consolation, it is that Werro, aged 22, clocked a championship record of 1:54.81 on a chilly, breezy evening in Birmingham to beat her. But warmer thoughts will be harder to find for Hodgkinson.

Instead, the Olympic champion must process the dawning of a serious rivalry and one that is not currently swinging in her favour. This one was settled by the margin of 0.2sec.

In the long run, Hodgkinson might view such moments as the competitive nectar needed for the breaching of new frontiers, of course, but the sting in the present will be real. Not many athletes have the finishing speed to match Hodgkinson, but in their past two races Werro has kicked away from her with the force of a donkey.

The decisive move here came after 500 metres, when Werro put the hammer down.

Hodgkinson, who had been near enough level at the bell after a 56sec opening lap, went with her, and they both separated from Femke Broeders-Bol in third, but the Brit had no answer. She never got her nose in front, and those moments of futility can leave lasting doubts in an athlete.

The 24-year-old, who was chasing a third straight European title, was evidently in little mood to indulge the celebrations of on-track interviewer Iwan Thomas. He assumed she would be thrilled with silver, but Hodgkinson responded: ‘I think I would be happier with a gold.’

Kely Hodgkinson was forced to settle for second in the women's 800m final on Friday

Hodgkinson jokingly took off her silver medal at the European Championships in Birmingham

She later added: ‘I think with that level of competition, any medal is a really good achievement and another one to add to my collection so I can never be disappointed with that. But I'm defending champion so I wanted to do that.

‘I knew it was going to come down to the wire but I really thought I was going to win today. But it wasn't meant to be. I didn't do anything wrong, it was just one of those things.

‘Congrats to Audrey. I am sure we will have more battles.’

That much seems certain. And for two women striving to break the oldest world record in track athletics, that will be a good thing.

But Werro has the edge. Having been beaten twice by Hodgkinson during the indoor portion of the season, she gained spectacular revenge in Stockholm in June when the Brit set a personal best of 1:54.33. Not only was that a win against a full-form Hodgkinson, Werro’s time of 1:53.98 was the third quickest in history. A month later, Werro ran quicker again with a 1:53.80 – if anyone is to better the dubious mark of 1:53.28 set by the Czech Jarmila Kratochvilova in the Eighties, Werro might have the edge.

To think, Werro was only cleared to race in this final on appeal after being tripped in her semi-final. It was a marginal call but also the correct one, so there should be no controversy around what it led to.

For Hodgkinson, the bigger picture will make for strange viewing. After the injury troubles of 2025, her times in 2026 have moved sharply on an upward trajectory, including the indoor world record in February, so she rightly resents any suggestion of ‘failure’ at losing a race or two. She was borderline tetchy in using that label prior to these Championships.

But in athletics, the clock is a secondary adversary to the field and Werro’s emergence is a huge fly in the ointment. For the rest of us watching, we can presumably take great pleasure in where it leads, because athletics needs rivalries. In these two gifted runners, it has one that has the potential to go on for years.

Sports.title: Supercomputer backs Arsenal to retain Premier League title, predicts how Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City will get on under new bosses - and names the surprise team in Europe who might get relegated
Sports.content:
Supercomputer backs Arsenal to retain Premier League title, predicts how Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City will get on under new bosses - and names the surprise team in Europe who might get relegated

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The opening day of the Premier League season is fast approaching, with a supercomputer backing Arsenal to defend their title in the 2026-27 campaign.

Mikel Arteta's side ended a 22-year wait to be crowned champions last term, with the Gunners holding off Man City after finishing as runners-up in three successive seasons.

Arteta will look to become just the fourth manager in Premier League history to retain the title, following Sir Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola.

According to Opta's supercomputer, which has conducted 10,000 data-led simulations of the campaign, Arsenal are the overwhelming favourites having been given a 38 per cent chance of lifting the trophy again in May.

By contrast, Liverpool were given a 28.5 per cent chance of retaining the title last year under Arne Slot, with the Reds ultimately finishing down in fifth.

A concern for Arsenal, however, has been highlighted over the back injury sustained by William Saliba with Arsenal's win percentage dropping from 68.7 to 47.6 per cent in the Premier League when the Frenchman is unavailable.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will look to be just the fourth boss to lead his side to back-to-back Premier League titles

Manchester City are seen as the second most likely team to be crowned champions

Man City are viewed as Arsenal's most likely challengers again, despite the departure of their legendary manager Pep Guardiola.

Enzo Maresca's side have been given a 20.5 per cent chance of glory following a summer of change, with Elliot Anderson the headline addition at £116m, although Rodri could follow Bernardo Silva in leaving the club.

PREMIER LEAGUE TITLE PROJECTION Arsenal – 38% Man City – 20.5% Liverpool – 9.2% Man United – 6.2% Aston Villa – 4.8% Chelsea – 4.1% Tottenham – 2.9% Source: Opta

Liverpool are third most likely champions at 9.2 per cent, despite new boss Andoni Iraola admitting in pre-season that his side 'cannot sustain the level we want' at this time.

The Reds are followed by rivals Manchester United, with Michael Carrick given a 6.2 per cent chance of winning the league.

Despite Aston Villa selling Morgan Rogers for a British transfer record £117million to Chelsea and the departure of Youri Tielemans to Man United, Unai Emery's side are fifth favourites at 4.8 per cent.

They are narrowly ahead of Chelsea under new boss Xabi Alonso at 4.1 per cent, with the Blues having a clear fixture schedule after missing out on Europe last season.

It is a similar situation at Tottenham, who are seen as having a 2.9 per cent chance of claiming the title under Roberto De Zerbi.

Tottenham have been among the biggest spenders in the transfer market this summer, with Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes among marquee signings at £100m and £85m respectively.

The spend comes with Spurs having recorded back-to-back 17th placed finishes in the top flight, with the Premier League status only confirmed on the final day of last season.

Hull City earned promotion to the top flight via the playoffs, but are seen as favourites to go down

Fulham are viewed as potential surprise strugglers under their new boss Alvaro Arbeloa

At the other end of the table, the three newly promoted sides have unsurprisingly been viewed as the most likely to go straight back down to the Championship.

Hull City, who came up from the play-offs, are deemed the most at risk of relegation at 38.7 per cent.

Ipswich and Coventry follow on 31.2 and 27.9 per cent, respectively.

The three clubs can take heart from Sunderland, who were viewed as the side most likely to finish bottom last season only for the Black Cats to qualify for Europe after a memorable campaign.

PREMIER LEAGUE RELEGATION RISK Hull City – 38.7% Ipswich Town – 31.2% Coventry City – 27.9% Sunderland – 25.9% Fulham – 23.4% Leeds United – 22.5% Crystal Palace – 20% Source: Opta

Sunderland's participation in the Europa League and their limited transfer activity this summer could have an impact on their prospects this campaign.

Opta's supercomputer has the Black Cats as fourth most likely club to be relegated at 25.9 per cent,

It follows Sunderland's underlying numbers last season, where they had the third lowest open-play expected goals, as well as facing the third-most shots and the fourth-most shots on target in the top flight.

Fulham are the next club at risk at 23.4 per cent, following a summer which has seen Marco Silva leave and be replaced by Alvaro Arbeloa.

Leeds United and Crystal Palace follow at 22.5 and 20 per cent, respectively.

Nottingham Forest and Brentford are next at 18.1 and 16.3, followed by Everton and Bournemouth on 13.6 and 13.1.

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes get off to worst possible start as a DRONE crashes into the track before hurdles event - with British star, 33, underwhelming after first day
Sports.content:
Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes get off to worst possible start as a DRONE crashes into the track before hurdles event - with British star, 33, underwhelming after first day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A drone crash was the least of Katarina Johnson-Thompson’s concerns as she made an underwhelming start to her challenge for a European Championship medal in Birmingham.

After three disciplines, the 33-year-old was placed 15th and offering little indication she has fully recovered race sharpness from the calf niggle that ruled her out of the Commonwealth Games.

Serving as a portent of the hiccups that lay ahead, Johnson-Thompson’s first event, the 100m hurdles, was delayed during surreal scenes when a drone fly-by went hilariously wrong. In attempting to pass underneath the barriers, the driver lost his bearings and crashed into one of the hurdles.

When the gun finally set the field loose, Johnson-Thompson clocked 14sec – her worst time in 14 years of competing in major championships. From there, she regained some ground by clearing 1.83m in the high jump, allowing the two-time world gold medallist to climb to 10th, before tumbling four spots with a disappointing 12.79m in the shot put – 165cm short of her best.

Poland’s Adrianna Sulek-Schubert leads from Ireland’s Kate O’Connor.

Meanwhile, World Athletics president Lord Sebastian Coe has played down rumours that low crowds in Birmingham could harm London’s bid to host the 2029 World Championships.

"Maybe we need a stretcher? Medics?" 🚨



This scenic drone shot was going so well... 💥🤕 pic.twitter.com/UJEIm32LhJ — BBC Sport (@BBCSport) August 14, 2026

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes got off to a strange start when her 100m hurdles race was delayed by a camera drone crash

The Alexander Stadium, with a capacity of 23,000, was almost half-empty during some sessions earlier in the week, which has sparked awkward questions at a time when UK Athletics is bidding against Rome, Nairobi and Munich for the bigger event in three years.

Asked if pictures of empty seats in Birmingham might influence panel members looking at London’s presentation, Lord Coe said: ‘Look, it’s horses for courses. We had London (Olympics) in 2012, London (world championships) in 2017, London will point to having sold out Diamond League five months before the event took place. So I think it was a challenge. It’s always a challenge starting a championship on a Monday morning.’

Sports.title: How 'Gladiator' Amy Hunt became Britain's newest sprint superstar - as self-styled 'track goddess' eyes fantastic four golds in Birmingham and nipping at the heels of the international elite
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The fingers told the story of Amy Hunt’s incomplete mission in Birmingham on Thursday evening. First, she showed two for the gold medals she has collected so far in her domination of European sprinting and then she held up four to signify a job half done.

Even in this city of bovine obsessions, there presumably isn’t a bull stubborn enough to wager against that target being met over the weekend.

On Saturday, she will team up with Dina Asher-Smith in the 4x100m, for which the British quartet are favourites, and they will go again in the mixed relay on Sunday. Given the male talent pool includes Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu, respectively the European gold and silver medallists, Hunt’s chances of delivering on her astonishing projections are more than strong.

By now, folk are aware enough of her remarkable talents, both for the winning of races over short distances and her willingness to accompany the golds with spoken nuggets. In an era when too many of her contemporaries hide their personalities behind thick shields, Hunt, 24, is the open book athletics needed; a Cambridge graduate who isn’t afraid to share idiosyncratic declarations of self-confidence and one who, repeatedly, has backed up big talk with big performances.

By Thursday night, with the 200m title added to the 100m gold won on Monday, she was channelling Russell Crowe’s Gladiator on the track with the cry: ‘Are you not entertained?’ It was later followed by a charming explanation to reporters that her father is so obsessed by the film that his parting words to his daughter, prior to each race, include another Maximus classic: ‘Strength and honour.’

Added to the 200m world silver medal Hunt in Tokyo last year, the honours are adding up. So too is the strength of conviction that Olympic prizes and Asher-Smith’s British sprint records could soon be under threat by the next British speedster off the rank.

Newly crowned double European sprint champion Amy Hunt is the open book that athletics needs

On Saturday, she will team up with Dina Asher-Smith in the 4x100m

Hunt signalled she is halfway to her target of four gold medals after adding 200m glory to her 100m triumph

It is an enticing thought, especially as we approach the halfway point of the LA Olympic cycle. But there are a couple of caveats at play – by timings, the best of Asher-Smith, 30, remains some way ahead of what we have seen so far from Hunt, and more pertinent, the places on an Olympic podium are further clear again.

Some context here: Hunt’s best at the 100m is 10.97sec, which was delivered in Stockholm earlier this year, and at the longer distance she clocked 22.08sec in Tokyo last year. Fast as the sporting world likes to move on, let’s not forget Asher-Smith went 0.15sec faster in winning the 100m world silver in 2019 and was 0.2sec quicker while winning 200m gold at the same championships.

Asher-Smith, a world-class athlete at her best and, more importantly, an expert at managing the rounds at a championship, is no soft target. In other words, Hunt will need to maintain this steep trajectory to even get close to breaking her national records.

The other conversation involves catching the world’s elite and perspective is needed – in 2026, when we have seen the best of Hunt in the 100m, she only ties 25th in the global list, more than 0.3sec off the top, and her standard for the 200m places her 10th, more than half a second off Julien Alfred.

The purpose of mentioning these deficits is not to dilute any hype, but an accurate scaling of where she stands when non-European bibs are in the race might be necessary. In doing so, it should also be recognised, with some excitement, that Hunt is not close to being the finished article. That is a good thing.

Adam Gemili, her former training partner and an excellent analyst of the biomechanics in sprinting, told the Daily Telegraph that he can foresee Hunt reaching the 21.6s in the 200m, her stronger discipline.

The long stride of a 5ft 11ins runner has a certain ring of Usain Bolt about it; the trade off is slower starts in the 100m, but there are those around UK Athletics who believe she can the top-end speeds of the best women in the world. On the latter, it was demonstrated in how she ran down the field in the shorter distance on Monday and again when she passed Asher-Smith on the straight on Thursday.

Hunt's best times are still slower than Dina Asher-Smith at her peak and improvement will be needed to catch the world's best

It is exciting that Hunt is not the finished article with Adam Gemili forecasting she can go 21.6s in the 200m

Those strengths offer fascinating possibilities, as does her comfort in the unique challenge of a championship, where the pressure is greatest and fatigue accumulates between rounds. As Hunt previously demonstrated by describing herself as an 'academic badass and track goddess', some athletes are more born to the spotlight than others. Lord Sebastian Coe, president of World Athletics, has been among the luminaries at the European Championships to identify that ease with her circumstances as a decisive trait.

Doubtless it will be tested in more extreme circumstances at the world championships next year, by which point more time will have been afforded to understanding Hunt’s peculiar issue with low blood pressure. She revealed it in the wake of winning the 200m, with the consequence that felt close to fainting during a race in London earlier this year. Less than ideal.

But Hunt has overcome all manner of problems to get this far. It should not be forgotten that after breaking the under-18 world record for the 200m, she spent years tormented by injuries. A ruptured quadricep while at university left her in such a state that she needed help from her mother to get out of the shower.

These days, she might require assistance carrying the medals and little else.

Sports.title: Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo signed prenup agreement with new wife Georgina Rodriguez, as marriage certificate and full details of their wedding at £30m mansion emerge
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez got married at their new £30million mansion near Lisbon in front of just four witnesses and their children, it emerged today.

Cristiano's doting mum Dolores Aveiro and his three siblings Hugo, Elma and Katia, were not present at the intimate civil ceremony, which took place at 1.30pm on Tuesday.

Georgina's sister Ivana, Cristiano's long-time friend Miguel Paixao and a Spanish couple named as Jose Rodriguez Sangil and his wife Monica Goncalez Martinez were the only witnesses.

Registrar Maria Manuel Ferreira de Campos Folhadela de Oliveira travelled from the northern Portuguese city of Porto to Cascais to officiate the ceremony.

And the star couple, who married exactly one year to the day after they announced their engagement on social media, have decided to keep their prenuptial assets separate despite tying the knot after a decade-long romance.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez married with four witnesses in Cascais, Lisbon

The marriage certificate for Ronaldo and Georgina's wedding has now emerged

The couple posted photos of them wearing their wedding rings after the small ceremony

They signed a prenup agreement to define their property regime on August 10, a day before the ceremony, at a public notary's office in Lisbon.

Cristiano Ronaldo's representatives confirmed earlier this week the footballer and his long-time partner married on August 11 in an 'intimate' ceremony in Cascais after the couple posted photos of them wearing their wedding rings on social media.

It followed speculation which turned out to be false that they were due to marry at Funchal Cathedral in Cristiano's native island of Madeira on Saturday.

No details had emerged about where in Cascais they had wed or who exactly was at the ceremony apart from their children.

Overnight respected Portuguese newspaper Jornal de Noticias published a copy of the marriage certificate showing it took place at Cristiano's massive mansion in the upmarket residential area of Quinta da Marina.

And it also evidenced the fact so few people were invited there appeared to be no place for Cristiano's mum, who gave the union her blessing shortly afterwards by posting a heart emoticon on her son's Instagram in response to his wedding announcement, or the rest of his family apart from his children.

Jose Rodriguez Sangil was described as a Spanish jeweller by Portuguese press.

The marriage document listed Cristiano's full name and age of 41 as well as his birthplace and the names of his parents, including his late father Jose Dinis.

Cristiano's massive built-from-scratch mansion in Quinta da Marina was the venue

The home boats an impressive infinity pool, underground car park and a private cinema room

Ronaldo wore his wedding ring on his finger as he returned to training in Saudi Arabia

The same details were listed for 32-year-old Georgina, born in the Argentinian capital Buenos Aires, and referenced by her full name of Georgina Luisa Rodriguez Hernandez. They will both keep their pre-marriage names.

The marriage certificate was recorded as number 1,493 of this year but appears to have been listed at Porto's Registry Office instead of Cascais which is the municipality where the wedding took place.

Cristiano and Georgina are now back in Saudi Arabia where the Portuguese international plays his club football for Al Nassr ahead of the start of the new season tomorrow.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes names £60m Arsenal star they should 'get rid of' instead of Myles Lewis-Skelly amid Man United and Chelsea links
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes names £60m Arsenal star they should 'get rid of' instead of Myles Lewis-Skelly amid Man United and Chelsea links

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Man United legend Paul Scholes believes Arsenal would be making a mistake if they sold Myles Lewis-Skelly this summer - and highlighted another player the Gunners should move on instead.

Lewis-Skelly, 19, enjoyed a breakout campaign in 2024-25, and while he struggled for gametime last time out, he played an important role in the end-of-season run-in.

However, with the £75million addition of Bruno Guimaraes adding to the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze as options in central midfield, it has raised uncertainty over the 19-year-old's future.

Reports then broke earlier this week suggesting Arsenal had offered Lewis-Skelly to both Chelsea and Man United.

And, speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet, Scholes felt that if Arsenal sanctioned his departure it would be a big mistake.

‘I prefer Myles Lewis-Skelly in centre midfield to Zubimendi,’ Scholes said.

Paul Scholes believes Arsenal would be making a mistake if they sold Myles Lewis-Skelly

Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a move to both Chelsea and Manchester United this summer

‘I think Zubimendi struggled last year. If there’s one player you are going to get rid of, it would be him [Martin Zubimendi].'

Scholes also pointed to a wider issue if Arsenal were to sell their academy graduate, who can play at left-back and in central midfield.

He added: 'It reminds me a little bit of when Danny Welbeck left Manchester United. I hated it, didn’t like it.

'Now, Danny was a little bit older than Myles Lewis-Skelly, but when you’re losing your own players, it’s disappointing.'

Jamie Carragher agreed with Scholes' thoughts and admitted he was left shocked by the reports.

He said 'Do you think it’s from his side or the club’s side? That’s the thing that was a little bit strange about it. It felt almost like Arsenal offered Manchester United Myles Lewis-Skelly.

'It wasn’t Myles Lewis-Skelly saying I want to leave or his people putting something out. That’s where the shock came from.

'I still can’t believe it. Obviously, last season wasn’t great for him for the whole season, but when a young player has already put in performances like I’ve seen him put in at the Bernabeu...

'He was running the game at the Bernabeu from left-back and then his performance in the Champions League final in central midfield against Paris Saint-Germain.'

Scholes felt Arsenal should move on Martin Zubimendi instead of the young Englishman

Carragher continued: 'You can’t play at that level unless you’re pretty special at that age. All young players have ups and downs. Last season he didn’t play as much as he probably would have liked.

'But, as you just said, his ceiling is so high for the performances he’s already put in as a kid. I couldn’t believe that Arsenal would even think about letting him go.'

When pressed on Lewis-Skelly's future earlier this week, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta refused to give anything away.

'I’m not going to talk about any speculation,' he said. ‘If there is a speculation about our players, that’s a good sign. That means that we attract attention and they’re doing a good job.’

Sports.title: Amazon's billionaire founder Jeff Bezos officially buys minority stake in Liverpool - as consortium's £1.65billion investment with ex-QPR owner Amit Bhatia is confirmed in Reds statement
Sports.content:
Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group have officially sold around a third of the club to a consortium of billionaires.

It is a mega-money deal that sees the Boston-based FSG, who also own baseball behemoths the Red Sox, set for a £1.65billion payout.

The consortium is led by former Queens Park Rangers supremo Amit Bhatia, with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos also indirectly involved — though the third-richest man in the world will not have a seat on the board.

Bhatia will become the club’s vice chairman.

Also on the consortium is technology pioneer Bryan Baum and Elaine Saverin, the wife of Facebook co-founder Eduardo who was Mark Zuckerberg’s class mate and business partner.

Mike Gordon, FSG President, said: 'Liverpool has always been built by thinking beyond one season and making decisions with the club's long-term interests in mind.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is part of a group to have bought a minority stake in Liverpool

Boston-based FSG, who also own baseball behemoths the Red Sox, are set for a £1.65billion payout

'That approach continues to attract interest from respected investors and business leaders around the world. As we considered this opportunity, it became clear that Amit and the consortium shared our long-term philosophy and appreciation for what makes Liverpool special.

Their experience and perspective will complement the strong foundation already in place, and we look forward to working together.'

Sources close to the deal and FSG suggest the move will not impact day-to-day running of the club and the relationship between the hierarchy and Bhatia, who has been in discussions for some time to make said purchase, may flexibly evolve over the years.

FSG maintain the keys to the club and are the majority owners who can make decisions, though Bhatia and his 1892 Holdings will be consulted on big decisions.

Bhatia believes that the consortium is a perfect mix of experience, relationships, contacts and reach across global business which will see them network into India and Asia.

Bhatia said: ‘We are incredibly proud to be investing in Liverpool Football Club and to be doing so alongside FSG. We have the utmost respect and admiration for FSG as owners and for everything they have achieved at Anfield.

'To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership, and we look forward to supporting the club's continued success for years to come.’

MEET THE KEY PLAYERS

JEFF BEZOS

Bezos is the third-richest man in the world, according to Forbes. In 1994, he read that web usage was growing at a rate of 2,300 per cent a year and wanted to open an online book store, so set one up in his garage in Seattle alongside his then wife Mackenzie Scott.

He changed the name from Cadabra to Amazon after the South American river as, at the time, website listings were alphabetised so an 'A' listing would be near the top. They slowly started selling more products and are now one of the most recognisable companies in the world.

Bezos is no longer the CEO of Amazon but retains the title of executive chairman. He is also the owner of the Washington Post and founder of Blue Origin which competes with Elon Musk in the modern-day space race. He flew to space in 2021.

The 62-year-old has dabbled in the idea of sports investment before. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

He married former American journalist Lauren Sanchez last year.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has dabbled with the idea of sports ownership in the past

EDUARDO SAVERIN

Saverin was born in Brazil with Romanian heritage. He moved to Miami at age 13 and attended Harvard University. He became friends with fellow undergraduate Mark Zuckerberg and the pair wanted to set up a website for students to communicate, making a $1,000 investment each.

The site was originally named 'The Facebook' and soon grew to other universities, later anyone in the world aged 13 or older. It now has more than 3billion users and its parent company, Meta Platforms, has a market value of around £1.12trillion.

Saverin is played by Andrew Garfield in The Social Network film based on the book Accidental Billionaires about his rise at Facebook. Weeks before Facebook became a public company, he moved to Singapore and renounced his US citizenship.

The 44-year-old is now head of B Capital, a venture capital firm.

Join the discussion How do you feel about foreign billionaires buying into historic English football clubs like Liverpool?

Eduardo Saverin was a co-founder of Facebook and is now head of venture capital firm B Capital

Amit Bhatia, the son in law of Lakshmi Mittal, previously worked for QPR for 19 years

AMIT BHATIA

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British-Indian with an investment banking background in sectors such as technology, media, property, real estate and health.

He formerly worked on Wall Street before founding a construction company aged 32, which has more than 5,000 UK employees. He won the young entrepreneur of the year award in 2013.

Bhatia married Vanisha Mittal in 2004 in a six-day wedding which the Guinness World Records recorded as the most-expensive ceremony of all time at £41m. Vanisha's father is Lakshmi Mittal, the world's 65th-richest man with £24.8bn as per Forbes.

Bhatia worked at QPR for 19 years and his company, AyBe Capital, owns shares in the cricket franchise London Spirit, former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen's YouTube channel and an indoor golf league founded by Rory McIlroy.

The tycoon recently played a round of golf with basketball legend LeBron James and is regularly on the course with Indian cricketing icon Sachin Tendulkar.

Sports.title: Finlay Tarling dead aged 19: British cyclist dies after serious accident during eighth stage of Volta a Portugal
Sports.content:
Finlay Tarling dead aged 19: British cyclist dies after serious accident during eighth stage of Volta a Portugal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

British cyclist Finlay Tarling has died today after a tragic accident during the Volta a Portugal.

The Welsh rider, 19, was on the eighth stage of the race when the incident occurred on a 166.8km route to Fafe, in the north of the country.

In a statement, his team NSN said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

'Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

'Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend.'

In a post on X, the Portuguese Cycling Federation spoke of their 'most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones'.

British cyclist Finlay Tarling died in a serious accident during a race in Portugal

The organisation added that the usual podium ceremony would not take place out of 'respect and mourning'.

Tarling's older brother Josh is a world champion cyclist on the track and a stage winner at last year's Giro d'Italia.

Portuguese newspaper RTP reported that the incident had allegedly been caused by a vehicle that was not involved in the race.

The report stated that the car had driven on the wrong side of the road and collided with Tarling, who had been behind the peloton.

The rider was reportedly given immediate medical attention but died shortly after the crash.

Portugal's president Antonio José Seguro said Tarling's death 'saddens the peloton, the race, and the country that welcomed him'.

He offered his 'deepest condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his teammates at NSN Development Team, and to the entire cycling community, joining in their grief with deep emotion'.

A statement from the International Cycling Union read: 'The UCI is deeply saddened by the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling, who passed away following a serious accident during today’s 8th stage of the Volta a Portugal.

'The UCI extends its deepest condolences to Finlay’s family, friends, and teammates.'

More to follow...

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson misses out European Championships gold medal in thrilling 800m final
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson misses out European Championships gold medal in thrilling 800m final

The women's 800m was one of the most anticipated events of the European Athletics Championships, as it promised a thrilling three-battle between Keely Hodgkinson, Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson went into the final as a two-time defending champion (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Great Britain's Keely Hodgkinson narrowly missed out a home gold medal in the women's 800m final at the European Athletics Championships. Hodgkinson, 24, came second behind the supreme Audrey Werro in her bid a three-time European champion at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham.

‌



Swiss sensation Werro recovered from a dramatic fall during her semi-final on Thursday afternoon to clinch the gold medal with a rapid time of 1:54.81. Hodgkinson made the fastest start under the Friday-night lights but had the 22-year-old on her shoulder.

‌



On the final lap, Werro made her move and gained the lead. Hodgkinson pushed to make it a dramatic finish but couldn't pip her rival to the finish line and had to settle for silver.

‌



Meanwhile, Femke Broeders-Bol set a new national record for the Netherlands as she earned bronze. Hodgkinson was all smiles after the final, although she jokingly took her silver medal off during an interview.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It was a great race, I love a good challenge and that's what it was," the Atherton-born star reflected. "I have mixed emotions. With that level of competition, any medal is a good achievement. Another one to add to my collection and I can never be disappointed with that.

"I knew it was going to come down to the wire and I really wanted to win. I guess it just wasn't meant to be. There were so many ways it could have played out. Audrey wanted to take it on, with that wind I was happy to let her. We are all great athletes and I look forward to the next match-up.

"I've said all year it's really motivating to be in such a competitive event. I love it, it's such a competitive event. I had a pretty good day, it just didn't quite go the way I wanted it to."

‌



View 2 Images Audrey Werro pipped Keely Hodgkinson to claim gold in Birmingham (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

As for Werro, who ran the fastest time for 43 years earlier this season, she picked up her first senior international gold medal. But the rising star's chances of even racing were plunged into doubt following her aforementioned fall.

Werro was holding the inside line in a crowded field before disaster struck, as she went down due to an 'unintentional touch' involving Werro and France's Anais Bourgoin. Following a review, Werro and Lithuania's Gabija Galvydyte were reinstated to the final.

Article continues below

The organisers explained: "The incident resulted in the fall of two athletes, Werro and Galvydyte. Having reviewed the circumstances, the referee decided to qualify both athletes in accordance with the applicable rules."

Reflecting on Werro's final performance, Paula Radcliffe told BBC One: "Audrey Werro is young still and that was a huge amount of pressure even without the fall, without the bruising and then to pull it together to take the race by the scruff of the neck, which I think Keely did intend for her to do but she thought she could come back at her. But Werro had another gear."

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez deadline passes as Chelsea reject transfer amid Man City interest
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez deadline passes as Chelsea reject transfer amid Man City interest

Enzo Fernandez is wanted by new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca and Chelsea set a strict deadline for any club to meet their £120million valuation by 5pm on Friday

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez's future remains undecided (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Chelsea expect Enzo Fernandez to remain at Stamford Bridge after their deadline for clubs to bid £120million passed without an offer. Fernandez, 25, is a top target for Manchester City with just over two weeks of the summer transfer window left.

‌



Former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca wants to reunite with the Argentine at City, who were told alongside other interested clubs that they had until 5pm UK time on Friday to meet his valuation. But it's understood that Chelsea have not received a bid.

‌



The Blues now expect Fernandez to be part of Xabi Alonso's squad after deadline day on September 1. City, however, don't believe the saga is over and that Chelsea would still be open to selling their vice-captain, who returned to training this week following the World Cup.

‌



City are looking to sign a replacement for star midfielder Rodri, who's edging closer to a move to Barcelona. Another City midfielder, Tijjani Reijnders, has agreed to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Qadsiah in a £52m deal.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Barca have made two offers for Rodri, the latest of which came in at £51m, after the 30-year-old agreed personal terms. But City held firm and turned down the proposal. Etihad chiefs are demanding £60m for Rodri, who's in the final year of his contract.

Maresca will take charge of his first competitive match as City boss on Sunday, as his side face Arsenal in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. During his pre-match press conference, the Italian said that he didn't anticipate any imminent arrivals, but reckons that City will make 'one or two' more signings before the window closes.

"For sure there are things that we need to do. How many, I don't know," Maresca admitted. "Could be one, could be two. Depends also if players leave.

‌



"Now, in this moment 48 hours before a final - my first final in this club - I will try to win the first trophy. First of all, the transfer window is open, we can buy players and we can sell players, anything can happen ... I just saw Rodri now in the building, I gave him a big hug, he looks good so we see what happens."

Is the Enzo Fernandez saga over? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez is back training with Chelsea (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



On Reijnders, he added: "It is not done officially, we will see in the next hours. I already spoke with him a few times in pre-season. We will see at the end if he is going to leave or going to stay.

"In the way he was playing in the pre-season games I was quite happy with his performances overall. I know Tij from Italy, from (AC) Milan when he was there, so I know him quite well.

"Probably there he was playing in a different position, he likes to play a little bit more deep than higher on the pitch. But again, in the pre-season he was good and now we see what happens and then we decide."

Sports.title: Inside Ruben Amorim's 14 months at Man Utd – Smashed TV, quit threats, Grimsby debacle
Sports.content:
Inside Ruben Amorim's 14 months at Man Utd – Smashed TV, quit threats, Grimsby debacle

Ruben Amorim is all set to face former club Manchester United with AC Milan, seven months after his turbulent Old Trafford tenure came to an end

View 5 Images Ruben Amorim endured a torrid 14 months as Manchester United manager (Image: Getty)

Ruben Amorim will be reunited with Manchester United on Saturday afternoon as his AC Milan side takes them on in a pre-season friendly. The Italian club appointed the Portuguese as their head coach in June, just five months after he was sacked by United following a disastrous spell in charge.

‌



The 41-year-old was highly thought of before taking the United job due to his success with Sporting CP and arrived bright-eyed and bushy-tailed. But thanks to his own actions and the wider chaos at the club, he endured a miserable time at Old Trafford.

‌



His opposite number in the dugout for Saturday's friendly is Michael Carrick, whose relative success with United since January has only evoked more negative feelings towards Amorim's own dismal reign.

‌



Ahead of what will surely be a strange reunion for the manager in Poland - and one he will be desperate to emerge victorious from- Mirror Football takes a look back at Amorim's turbulent reign as United boss and how his time with the club unravelled.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

Smashed TV

Having left his top-of-the-table Sporting side in November 2024 to join United mid-season, Amorim quickly realised the monumental scale of his task. A 3-1 home defeat to Brighton in January 2025 marked a seventh loss in his first 15 games in charge.

‌



View 5 Images Amorim had to apologise for his outburst (Image: Getty)

The impact of that on the initially charismatic manager was clear to see as he cut a miserable figure both on the touchline and during post-match interviews. After the loss, Amorim branded his United team the worst in the club's 147-year history - something he quickly admitted he shouldn't have said.

His brutal comments demonstrated his frustration with the lack of progress as United's players failed to adapt to his much-criticised 3-4-2-1 formation. That frustration also spilt out in the dressing room as he damaged a TV used for tactics at half-time in a display of fury.

‌



Whilst he later took responsibility and admitted he would try to do better as a young head coach, the two incidents showed a degree of volatility. They raised questions about whether he had the necessary man-management skills to oversee the difficult project ahead of him, sowing the seeds of future struggles.

Europa League final heartbreak

As the season wore on, United's dreadful form made it increasingly clear that they would not qualify for Europe for the 2025/26 campaign via the Premier League. Winning the Europa League, of which they had reached the final, became of the utmost importance for securing Champions League qualification and getting the club back on the right trajectory.

View 5 Images United finished as runners-up in the Europa League (Image: Getty)

‌



However, Amorim's side showed very little quality in the Bilbao showpiece and were not helped by his selection decisions, including leaving Alejandro Garnacho and Kobbie Mainoo out of the starting line-up. Tottenham secured a 1-0 victory and ended a 17-year trophy drought.

The defeat, along with a 15th-place finish in the league, was a humiliating end to an already exhausting and miserable campaign. Amorim's rigid tactics, questionable man-management and overall negative demeanour led many in the media to demand his sacking. Amorim even said he was willing to walk away the very next day if that's what the board desired.

"In this moment, I am not going to be here defending myself, [it] is not my style," he said. "I cannot do it, is really hard for me. So I have nothing to show to the fans to say I am going to improve because of this, I had these problems, I will not do nothing.

‌



"In this moment, it's a little bit of faith. So let's see. Like I said before, coming here before in the flash, I am always open. If the board and fans feel that I'm not the right guy, I will go the next day without any conversation about compensation. But I will not quit again. I am really confident in my job and, as you can see, I will not change nothing in the way I do things."

INEOS and the United board were desperate to break the club's decade-long cycle of sacking managers every 18-24 months. They stuck with him, believing he deserved a full pre-season and a summer transfer window to shape the squad to his own preference. Crucially, he also still seemed to have the support of the majority of his players.

Grimsby Town debacle

Following a summer where United notably backed him by signing three high-quality forwards in Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, fans expected to see improvements. But after a defeat to Arsenal and a draw at Fulham came perhaps the lowest point in Amorim's United career.

‌



View 5 Images Pressure mounted on Amorim following United's defeat at Grimsby (Image: Getty)

In August 2025, United suffered a shock defeat to League Two side Grimsby Town in the Carabao Cup second round. As his side lost the penalty shootout, images of Amorim hunkering in the dugout rather than showing real leadership became ingrained in viewers' minds.

Memes of him fiddling with his tactics boards against the lower-league opposition also went viral on social media and cries of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the home crowd marked the ultimate humiliation.

‌



Having managed just 17 wins across 45 games. Amorim cut a defeated figure post-match, adding to a sense of foreboding. He said when asked if he understood what had happened at Blundell Park: "No. But I'm the manager. It should be my job to understand what happened." That only added to the general feeling that the United boss was already signalling he was ready to leave.

Quit threats and exit

A period of good form in October proved to be merely a brief respite and poor results quickly returned, with United again finding themselves on a winless run at the turn of the year. His self-deprecating comments, which had become more evident throughout his tenure, became an acceptance that his time at United was destined to be cut short.

He had said earlier in the season: "Sometimes I want to quit, sometimes I want to be here for 20 years, sometimes I love to be with my players, sometimes I don't want to be with them. So, again, I need to improve on that. It's going to be hard. But now I'm good with the next one."

‌



View 5 Images The manager's sacking seemed only a matter of time (Image: Getty)

In the new year, he began to more obviously call out United's hierarchy, seemingly egging them on to scrap his contract. Things came to a head after a 1-1 draw at Elland Road, in what would prove to be his final post-match outburst as the man in charge at Old Trafford.

"I came here to be the manager of Manchester United, not to be the coach of Manchester United. That is clear," Amorim said. "I know that my name is not [Thomas] Tuchel, it's not [Antonio] Conte, it's not [Jose] Mourinho, but I'm the manager of Manchester United. And it's going to be like this for 18 months or when the board decides to change.

‌



"I'm not going to quit. I will do my job until another guy is coming here to replace me. I just want to say that I'm going to be the manager of this team, not just the coach. I was really clear on that. That is going to finish in 18 months, and then everyone is going to move on. Thank you, guys."

United's higher-ups ultimately decided enough was enough and dismissed him the following day, putting an end to his miserable tenure. Under-18s coach Darren Fletcher was brought in as caretaker boss with the club sitting in sixth place.

Carrick stepped in later that month and changed United's fortunes. It is very difficult to imagine the team ever securing Champions League qualification with Amorim at the helm. Now, things will go full circle as the Portuguese boss takes on the man who ultimately supplanted him.

Sports.title: Championship 1-24 predictions: Every club's finishing place this season decided
Sports.content:
The most unpredictable, chaotic league in the world is officially back tonight, with Wolves and Blackburn kicking us off at Molineux.

Between now and May, 24 teams will battle it out over 46 gameweeks for a chance to land a golden ticket to the Premier League. Two will succeed with another joining them following an extended play-off campaign (don't forget it's now the top eight!). Three other teams will also exit the Championship, albeit through the trapdoor.

We all know from experience how gruelling and unpredictable the Championship is. So it's only logical that, for the second year running, I take a stab at calling where every team will finish.

Check out our 1-24 predictions below ahead of the big kick-off...

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

24 - Bolton Wanderers

I'm backing two of the promoted teams to stay up this year, or at the very least make a good fist of doing so. I'm less optimistic on Bolton, largely because in Amario Cozier-Duberry and Mason Burstow, they will have to make do without two of their most influential attackers from last season. It also feels like a lack of business has been done, particularly in those forward areas.

Ryan Hardie was signed on loan earlier this week and has double figure pedigree at this level but goals may still be hard to come by with loanees Cozier-Duberry and Burstow (their top scorer last term with 12 league goals) not returning. Sam Dalby was next best in the scoring charts with 10 goals but is an unknown quantity at this level. It feels like more firepower is essential before the transfer deadline. David Watson, Ben Davies, Akin Famewo, Luca Stephenson, Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal have all come through the door but none really jump out at you. If any team needs a big final few weeks in the window, it's Bolton.

‌



23 - Charlton Athletic

Charlton got over the line last year after a bit of a slog to give themselves an opportunity to kick on under Nathan Jones. The issue is that they will have to try and do so in a division which feels significantly stronger this time around - and I'm not totally sold on the business they've done being enough to keep their heads above water.

Jones has spoken about Charlton wanting to evolve but it's hard to see where the goals are coming from for them to do so. The Addicks were the third lowest scorers in the division last year; other than Charlie Kelman (7) and Sonny Carey (8) no other Charlton player registered more than three goals in the league. Millenic Alli and Karlan Grant have been brought in to add to Charlton's wide attacking options but the former has a dearth of Championship experience and Grant last hit double figures in the league back in the 2021-22 campaign. Their midfield options don't inspire confidence either; it's one thing questioning whether the strikers can get more goals but the service into them also needs to be better. I'm not seeing that correlation right now.

Charlton will be solid and diligent but I don't think that will be enough. It feels like Jones recognises that with his desire for Charlton to be less limited this year. Have they done the business to do so? It doesn't feel like it.

‌



22 - Lincoln City

View 7 Images Lincoln City went 29 games unbeaten to romp League One last season (Image: PA)

Momentum can be a force of nature in football and it half feels like Lincoln have forgotten how to lose games after going 29 unbeaten to absolutely romp their way to the League One title. But even for one of the most sensible and well-run clubs in the pyramid, take away your manager and star player from that formula and it's a pretty devastating one-two.

The reason I have them in the final relegation spot is that I fancy them to at least give a good fist of upsetting the odds again. However, Jack Moylan was their talisman and his loss is significant, maybe more so than Michael Skubala. On the incoming front, it feels like Tanto Olaofe has the tools to make a nuisance of himself at this level even if he may not be prolific. Mason Melia, the promising young Tottenham striker, is a wildcard in attack after signing on loan. There's not been loads of business done but Lincoln do still have the nucleus of the team that absolutely demolished League One last season.

‌



The step up will be significant and they will undoubtedly become reacquainted with the feeling that comes after losing games. But Lincoln can hold their own and will bloody some noses.

21 - Blackburn Rovers

Blackburn have arguably had the weakest transfer window of any side in the division, adding just Moussa Baradji, Jayden Fevrier and Sam Morsy to a squad that flirted with relegation for most of last season. Already, we're in alarm bell territory.

Tony Mowbray returning to Ewood Park has probably been Blackburn's most significant capture of the summer but the squad he will start the season with is threadbare. Rovers will play on the front foot more under Mowbray and have players who can outscore teams; that will be what sets them apart from others down the bottom. The fact they have attacking players who you would genuinely back to deliver over the course of a season, like Ryoya Morishita, Andri Gudjohnsen and Yuki Ohashi, is encouraging. But they lack depth in other areas and that will prove problematic as the season goes in.

‌



20 - Portsmouth

After two consecutive survival battles, it feels like Portsmouth are trying to kick on this summer by opening up the purse strings, operating at a different level in the transfer market compared to what we have seen previously. Big striker Marko Milovanovic and the all-action midfielder Rocco Shein after intriguing pick ups and the onus will be on the former to hit the ground running to ease some of the goal-scoring burden on Adrian Segecic, who is a right player. A fit and firing Josh Murphy will also go some way to helping on the goal front; plagued by injuries last year, he racked up 22 goal contributions in 45 league games during the 2024-25 campaign.

I think Portsmouth will be okay but I don't see them having the depth to climb the table significantly compared to last year. A lot will hinge on how their new signings adapt. We've seen lots of clubs, Millwall most recently, enjoy success from overseas signings and effective player trading. This year could be Portsmouth's first step in emulating that model, which would serve them well.

19 - Stoke City

‌



It almost feels like Stoke are stuck in some weird sort of Narnia whereby they do business I like each summer but don't tend to go anywhere. Therefore I just can't bring myself to back them for any sort of decent finish.

It's now been nine years since Stoke dropped out of the Premier League and they still haven't recorded a top-half finish in the Championship. Ethan Galbraith quickly established himself as one of the Championship's best playmakers at Swansea after making the step up from Leyton Orient last summer and landing him for big money felt like a real statement of intent at the time. But beyond that I'm not sold on any of their other incoming business. Viktor Johanssen and Million Manhoef are quality and Mark Robins should, theoretically, be the perfect manager to finally get Stoke out of their 14th-18th malaise. Maybe this will be the year. But it'll be a braver man than me who backs it.

18 - Preston North End

A Championship without Preston North End just doesn't feel right. I did initially have fears that could change, but late transfer business has convinced me to nudge them up this list.

‌



Ambition wise, PNE smashed their transfer record to retain the services of star man Alfie Devine after his stellar loan last year earlier this summer. But beyond that, it all felt a bit underwhelming for a while. Delano Burgzorg managed just three Championship goals last season and five the year before, while Jusef Erabi, also joining in attack, is an unknown quantity at this level. Captain Ben Whiteman chucking the towel in a fortnight before the season starts following interest from Wrexham is hardly a resounding vote of confidence for where PNE were at, either.

But they have replaced him swiftly with Leo Leroy from Basel, who looks a good signing. And it was confirmed on Friday that a deal for Stan Mills to join the club in January has been agreed due to Oxford United's current transfer embargo. More could follow before the window shuts. So although the vibes at Deepdale haven't been great throughout the summer, I don't see them in a relegation fight.

17 - Cardiff City

View 7 Images Cardiff City are back in the Championship after winning promotion last season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

‌



Cardiff look by far the best equipped of the promoted sides to cope with life in the Championship and I debated placing the Bluebirds a fair bit higher on the list here. I always think this pool of teams, the ones who won't be troubled by relegation but are perhaps unlikely to mount a realistic play-off push, are the hardest ones to place.

Brian Barry-Murphy's total football should translate well to a higher level and in Yousef Salech they boast a striker whose game will suit the league. Moylan is another player I fancy to replicate his stunning League One form in the Championship, while signing Nathan Trott permanently is huge after his excellent loan last season. Maybe Cardiff can maintain their momentum from last season and push for a higher finish than this. There has also been talk of significant further spending in the transfer market, which could skew these predictions. One thing I am certain of is they won't be looking anxiously over their shoulder.

16 - Watford

Individually, Watford have some proper talent in their squad. But they are another team that you just wouldn't feel comfortable backing to achieve something based on a lots of factors. One big one is the manager: Alessio Dionisi starts the season, but will he end it? Who knows. Probably not even Watford.

‌



Giorgi Chakvetadze and Nestory Irankunda (who is finalising a move to Sporting Lisbon as I finish these predictions) are big losses. Imran Louza would be another with intense speculation over his future. That would be three big losses and probably kill off any outside chance of a play-off push. That being said, who really knows what any season holds for Watford. The only thing I'll stick my neck out and say is that, like Cardiff above, they won't be looking over their shoulder at any point.

15 - Birmingham City

Birmingham will have grand ambitions this season and will be all the better for last year's campaign, where they consolidated themselves in steady if not spectacular fashion. The problem I think they'll find is that there are just too many teams who are better than them currently for them to really kick on this year.

Maybe that sounds harsh. Or lazy. Or both! But I just don't see the significant upturn in points they will require to break into the top eight, although they do have the scope to do something completely bonkers in the final weeks of the transfer window to make me look foolish.

‌



14 - Derby County

Derby came close to the play-offs under John Eustace last year and the nucleus of that squad is still intact. But I think they will be one of the teams who find themselves finishing lower this term simply due to the strength of others.

The unexpected collapse of a takeover by the Saudi Arabian boxing kingpin Turki Alalshikh is likely to have an impact on the club's incoming transfer activity, though they have managed to secure the permanent signings of popular loanees Sammy Szmodics and Bobby Clark. Derby are a strong, powerful team who nobody will fancy playing. And on their day, they are a match for any team in the division. Across the course of a season is another matter, though I wouldn't be too shocked if any of the teams placed between 10 and 14 here end up in slightly different spots.

13 - Bristol City

‌



It felt like Bristol City needed a big summer after falling away bigtime last year and, on paper, they've delivered. They've spent the best part of £9million on League One's two top strikers in Dom Ballard and Lorent Tolaj. Plus they've brought in the highly-rated Sam Tickle as their new No 1 keeper, the industrious Sam Greenwood to further strengthen in the attacking areas and Championship stalwart Jed Wallace. On paper, not bad, right?

Does all that equate to a play-off finish under the guidance of new head coach, Michael Skubala? Maybe. I still reckon Bristol City fall just short, mainly due to the strength of the division. There are just too many good teams ahead of them and, let's not forget, they are effectively ripping things up and starting again with Skubala at the helm. A top eight finish at the first time of asking is probably a stretch, but a good season here should set them up nicely for next year.

12 - West Brom

View 7 Images James Morrison will lead West Brom permanently after keeping them up last season (Image: Adam Fradgley/West Bromwich Albion FC)

‌



James Morrison is one of the big unknown quantities ahead of the new season. His arrival as caretaker boss was the catalyst for West Brom retaining their Championship status after a truly chastening campaign He rightly landed the job on a full-time basis off the back of that, but can he now oversee a promotion challenge?

The Baggies went back to basics under Morrison in a bid to accumulate the points necessary to stay afloat and it remains to be seen if they will stick with the same approach given the former midfielder has now effectively been given a blank canvas to work with. Squad-wise, West Brom have good players and better depth than some others. Does that translate into a top eight finish? I'm unsure, so I'll hedge my bets.

11 - Swansea City

Swansea start the season with perhaps the best striker in the division in Zan Vipotnik. But will they end the window with last season's Championship top scorer still in tow with Hull City circling? That remains to be seen and plays a factor here.

‌



Keeping Vipotnik would be a major transfer win and they've done smart business too: Elijah Just looked a right player at the World Cup and will bolster their attack and if they can keep Ross Stewart fit after snapping the striker up from Sunderland, then it could be the signing of the summer. Unfortunately, it's at the other end Swansea look less convincing. The news on the eve of the new season that Cameron Burgess has suffered an ACL injury isn't particularly helpful for Vitor Matos.

10 - Wrexham

Wrexham came agonisingly close to landing a play-off spot last season and will be in the mix to go one better this season. But again, the quality of the other teams pushing for those top eight positions could just nudge Phil Parkinson's team aside.

After hitting their stride in the second half of last term, Wrexham have opted for continuity and strengthened smartly rather than opting for full-scale surgery. Danny Imray is an excellent pick-up at right-back and will enhance their attacking threat from that area. Anthony Patterson will come in as first-choice keeper and is an upgrade on last season. Josh Windass will lead from the front again after bagging an impressive 17 goals last season with only Vipotnik, Ollie McBurnie and Haji Wright netting more. Kieffer Moore and Sam Smith will provide support but I reckon a marquee addition in attack is needed for them to gatecrash the top eight this time.

‌



9 - QPR

View 7 Images QPR could be dark horses for a top eight finish (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

In terms of transfer window wins, QPR are right up there. Looking at their business, there is a lot to like: Pierce Charles on loan feels shrewd, albeit the youngster dropped a clanger in the cup game with Millwall. Picking up Dennis Cirkin on a free transfer is just tremendous business and Tariq Lamptey could still be a game-changer if he can rediscover his fitness and hit top form again. Glenn Kamara also adds some steel in midfield.

The bonus QPR have despite their form absolutely falling off a cliff at the end of last season (and largely why I'm choosing to ignore that) is that they already have an adequate attacking arsenal to compliment their new signings. Richard Kone and Rumarn Burrell should both be in the goals after acclimatising to Championship level last term and are backed up by the likes of Karomoko Dembele, Kwame Poku and Koki Saito. And Illias Chair. What does that all up to? My prediction is QPR will be a good watch and dark horses for a top eight finish.

‌



8 - Sheffield United

Sheffield United were an absolute calamity last season and probably ruined many an ante-post bet. They were steady if unspectacular following Chris Wilder's return and feel safer to back this time around, albeit with the caveat that troubling the top two feels beyond them.

The incoming business so far doesn't feel like much to crow about, while the sale of Andre Brooks to Norwich was a painful one. But the team that finished the season is far superior than their final league standing of 13th. This time around, Wilder and Co won't be playing catch up after the sort of nightmare start even a depressed supercomputer would struggle to realistically muster up. They've lost Gustavo Hamer, but the squad still boasts plenty of firepower and players who have experience of doing the business at this level. Defensively they have some of the division's top performers in their respective positions in keeper Michael Cooper, Japhet Tanganga and Femi Seriki. That's a nice mix and I reckon they return to the pack challenging for promotion.

7 - Burnley

‌



Of all the relegated sides, Burnley feel like the hardest to predict. They are not the only club to head into the season with a manager who is untested on these shores but it feels like Nicky Hayen has a bigger job on his hands than Cesar Peixoto. If they retain the services of Zian Flemming, then Burnley could finish higher. They absolutely haemorrhaged goals last season - almost two a game - but I like the loan signing of Max Alleyne from Manchester City.

Cards on the table time: I really don't know what to expect from Burnley and they were by far the hardest to place on this list. My gut and head says they will not be the force they usually are in this division after dropping down. I had a couple of absolute shockers last year and Burnley could very well be the shout I try to avoid looking at for the next 12 months.

6 - Millwall

Millwall enjoyed their best campaign in a generation last time out as they defied all the odds to finish third, missing out on automatic promotion on the final day. Emulating that feat will take some doing, even though the nucleus of the squad that won more games than any other team in the division bar champions Coventry City largely remains.

‌



Talisman Femi Azeez is likely to depart and losing his ability to conjure up something from nothing in the final third will hurt a team who were the lowest scorers in the top eight. On paper, Millwall's incoming business looks positive and you can tell from their recent track record in the transfer market that they generally know what they're doing on that front. They also boast one of the division's top managers in Alex Neil, who underlined his credentials with last year's showing. The squad does feel imbalanced, though, with just two out and out senior wingers in Azeez and Kyrell Lisbie. And with Azeez likely to depart and Tristan Crama recently undergoing ankle surgery, Millwall will be without the dynamic right hand pairing that was so influential last term.

The Lions may not finish as high as last year, but another play-off finish feels within reach and would represent another strong season.

5 - Southampton

View 7 Images Tonda Eckert remains in charge of Southampton but he could face a ban over 'Spygate' (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

‌



Southampton were absolutely motoring at the end of last season and probably have the squad to finish better than the fifth place I've got them down for. But the uncertainty over Tonda Eckert plays a big role in that; if the German is handed a ban for the Spygate scandal that marred last year's play-offs, then that could skew Southampton's season massively. The shadow of that possibility even hanging over them might even do the trick.

Regardless of who is at the helm, Southampton won't be on minus points for long and will be among the teams slugging it out for promotion. It's hard to pinpoint a weakness in the squad: Daniel Peretz is back permanently and we already know his quality, while Cyle Larin, Lewis Dobbin and Divin Mubama give the Saints even more firepower. The squad is just a joke all around, really. Leo Scienza and Tom Fellows on either flank...forget the spying, are we sure that's allowed? Really, it's a poor season for Southampton if they are in the play-off eliminators. If the Eckert situation had been resolved and there was clarity on that front, I've have them well clear of them.

4 - Norwich City

Under Philippe Clement, Norwich feel like proper promotion contenders. The former Rangers boss inherited a team in turmoil with Norwich second from bottom after failing to win a staggering seven straight home games in the Championship. He would oversee 17 wins from 31 games, which is promotion form.

‌



I feel like a broken record banging on about strikers and firepower, but goals win prizes and Norwich have some seriously heavy artillery up top. Jovon Mokoma is the business and should be a decent shout for top scorer, while Mo Toure has adapted to the Championship seamlessly. Norwich are less convincing at the other end and will ship goals. But for every goal they concede they could go and score three. I can see them troubling the top, top dogs but having to settle for a play-off spot, eventually. Again, think they will be a really good watch for any neutrals who find themselves flicking through Sky Sports + via the red button on midweeks.

3 - West Ham

I know, I know: West Ham was the banker. This was the no-brainer, the one that couldn't fail etc etc. If we're speaking about absolute jokes of a squad then West Ham are bang up there in terms of invidual players (Jarrod Bowen in the Champ? Come on). And yet I think that's also part of the reason why a top two finish could elude them. They have the tools to succeed but does it all work together?

Nuno Espirito Santo has been there, done that, got that t-shirt when it comes to promotion from the Championship, so he's not walking into the unknown. But the landscape has changed drastically since then. West Ham in the Championship now feels far more significant than it did when they were last in here more than a decade ago and the dynamics have shifted; if they attempt to continue with the same pragmatic style Nuno has typically deployed throughout his career, then I don't see them doing enough to crack the top two. And that's before we even touch on the weight of expectation that will be on them and their manager. With respect, Wolves in the Championship at the time was a big job. But this feels like another level for him and a group of players who went down last year.

‌



I don't mean to go into full-on cliche mode, but how will this star-studded squad cope with being the scalp of the division? Can they, in fact, do it on a cold Tuesday night away at Stoke? Maybe I'm wrong and West Ham will absolutely romp it. But coming off the back of a bruising relegation and with off-field drama still prevalent in the background, I'm not sure it'll be as straightforward as some are expecting.

2 - Middlesbrough

You've got to give it to Boro - they have had the sort of transfer window that wouldn't look out of place in Football Manager (the good ones, not 2026). They've scooped major windfalls from sell-on clauses, banked a tidy sum from the sale of their talisman Hayden Hackney (bittersweet but necessary as his deal was up next year) and they've used it to level up in the two positions that cost them automatic promotion last year in goalkeeper and striker.

Radek Vitek is a huge upgrade on Sol Brynn and will be one of the division's top keepers, while Will Lankshear should absolutely feast if he is served up the same number of quality chances that Boro's forward's spurned last season. Just the impact from those two alone will serve Boro incredibly well. We know the squad is strong, even though the loss of Hackney is a huge blow.

‌



Backing Boro to finish second ahead of some of the other quality teams in this league might feel bold, but the team and manager Kim Hellberg are impressive. And while others, like the teams coming down, may have to find their feet back at the level, Middlesbrough should get motoring far quicker.

1 - Wolves

View 7 Images Wolves are likely to be in the frame for an instant return to the Premier League (Image: David Rogers)

Wolves needed a huge revamp after one of the worst Premier League seasons in history…that hasn’t happened. Wolves needed to shift the deadwood and high earners out of the club…that hasn’t happened either. So why - I hear you ask - are we tipping Cesar Peixoto’s side to finish at the top of the Championship pile?

‌



Simply put, Wolves have an embarrassment of riches for the second tier. In midfield, they have a Brazilian international in Andre, the exciting Fer Lopez and potentially Jordan James. Signing Kieran Trippier was an impressive coup, bringing Raul Jimenez back to Molineux was potentially even more eye-catching. Adam Armstrong, who was on course to be the league’s top scorer before moving to Molineux in the 2025/26 campaign, may have to settle for a place on the bench this time around.

Pre-season has shown Wolves will play on the front foot and press high, a method which has worked for previous title winners. They will need to start well to ease the toxicity and could still do with a new keeper and centre back, but Wolves will fancy their chances of lifting the trophy next May.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives injury update on five Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gives injury update on five Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield

Mikel Arteta was without five key players during pre-season but will able to welcome back three of them for Arsenal's clash with Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday

View 2 Images Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka have returned to Arsenal training (Image: Manuel Velasquez - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka will all be available to face Manchester City in the Community Shield. The Arsenal boss also provided updates on William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, who are both recovering from long-term injuries which they suffered during the World Cup.

‌



All five players didn't feature in any of the Gunners' pre-season friendlies. Rice, Zubimendi and Saka each made it to the final weekend of the tournament with England and Spain respectively, so they were afforded additional time off in order prepare for what's set to be another gruelling campaign at club level.

‌



Saliba, however, went down with a back problem in the opening stages of France's semi-final defeat to Spain. Meanwhile, Timber picked up a serious groin injury just days before the Netherlands kicked off their campaign.

‌



Arteta was asked to provide an update on the quintet during Friday's pre-match conference and had mixed news. "They [Rice, Zubimendi and Saka] will be available. They trained with us today, they will train tomorrow and if they are in the condition that we expect them to be, they will be involved."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The Arsenal manager added: "Jurrien is progressing really well, he is on the pitch, we are ramping up now with certain actions and especially the volume and the load. I think he is on a good trajectory, but there is still a few weeks to go. Wilo, as we all know, it's more a long-term injury."

Asked whether Timber could return before the next international break which starts in September and runs into October, Arteta replied: "We have to wait and see. He needs to start to train with the group in the next week or so hopefully, and then see how he progresses from there.

"It's been a long-term issue, and we want to make sure that every step that we take is the right one, he feels right to do that, because he's such an important player for us."

‌



How should Arsenal line up against Manchester City? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images William Saliba's back injury could rule him out for months (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

Both Rice and Saka had fitness issues during the World Cup and had to be managed by England's medical staff. But Arteta hasn't seen anything from the duo that's worried him.

‌



"We haven't noticed anything; they had individual plans through the time that they had with the national team," he explained. "They've been trying to evolve those issues and they have improved.

"In the rest period that they had, they both had specific programmes for themselves. They've been doing those and so far, what I saw the last two or three days, it was really good."
